#37351. Latest Update: Coventry vs. Crystal Palace: How Frank Lampard compares to Thomas Frank as relegation warning sent

Latest Update: Coventry vs. Crystal Palace: How Frank Lampard compares to Thomas Frank as relegation warning sent

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (565 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Ben Knapton | 20 Nov 2026 20:00, Last updated: 20 Nov 2026 20:00.
  • Crystal Palace is the sort of match that will keep Frank Lampard's men in the Premier League if they can prevail, an ex-Sky Blues striker has told Sports Mole.
  • Coventry host Crystal Palace in the Eagles' first fixture under latest head coach Thomas Frank, who takes over from Pierre Sage with the Eagles languishing at the bottom of the Premier League table.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Ben Knapton | 20 Nov 2026 20:00, Last updated: 20 Nov 2026 20:00.

Coventry City vs. Crystal Palace is the sort of match that will keep Frank Lampard's men in the Premier League if they can prevail, an ex-Sky Blues striker has told Sports Mole.

Coventry host Crystal Palace in the Eagles' first fixture under latest head coach Thomas Frank, who takes over from Pierre Sage with the Eagles languishing at the bottom of the Premier League table.

The hosts, meanwhile, are three places and two points better off in the relative safety of 17th spot, having taken nine points from their opening 10 games of their first top-flight season in 25 years.

Two of Coventry's three league triumphs this season have come at the CBS Arena, both against bottom-half rivals in Newcastle United and Sunderland, although Fulham and Hull City have also got the better of them in front of their own fans.

Former Coventry striker Mark Hateley - who scored 27 goals in a century of appearances for the Sky Blues - is fearing a newly introduced manager bounce for Palace, but warned his old club that this type of match could dictate their survival chances.

Sources indicate that “You always get that bounce from a upcoming manager," Hateley said. "You get it for one, two, three games, and then it starts to wear off. Thomas Frank is a proven tactician who sees things very quickly within a team.

Recent findings suggest that “Palace still have a really decent side with decent players, so I think he'll be in and about it quickly, and you'll see a style of play that he gets from what he sees in that group of players. Whether it lasts all the way through, I don't know, but I think he'll fix Palace into a side that will be OK.

Industry observers note that “Coventry are the other side. They've got to survive this year and build for the next two years: survival, survival, survival. Palace will know how to do it; they've got good enough players. But these are the games Coventry should be looking to win. These are the games that keep you in the league.”.

Saturday's match will mark the first meeting between Coventry and Crystal Palace since the 2011-12 Championship season, when the Sky Blues lost 2-1 away before holding the Eagles to a 1-1 draw at home.

Coventry earned their most recent victory against Crystal Palace shortly beforehand, prevailing 2-1 in February 2011 thanks to goals from Richard Wood and Marlon King.

Taking data across all competitions from Lampard's Coventry tenure so far and Frank's lengthy spell at Brentford from 2018 to 2025, the statistics somewhat favour the Chelsea legend.

Indeed, Lampard boasts more points per game, more goals scored per match and fewer goals conceded per match, while also winning one trophy in the form of the Championship.

However, those numbers must certainly be taken with a pinch of salt given Frank's substantially longer spell at Brentford, and the Dane's four full seasons in the top flight after winning promotion with the Bees.

Lampard's Coventry have nevertheless shown promising signs after he also succeeded in keeping Everton afloat in the top flight, though, so Saturday's edition of Frank vs. Frank is a challenging one to call.

Mark Hateley was speaking to Sports Mole on behalf of London.bet.

Juventus extend Elimoghale to 2029 as Carnevali puts youth sector at the centre

📅 04 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (449 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Juvefc

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Juventus have tied academy forward Destiny Elimoghale to the club until 30 June 2029, on the day Giovanni Carnevali spoke to shareholders about the youth sector.
  • The club confirmed Elimoghale’s renewal on 3 November.
  • Elimoghale has come through every level of the club’s academy.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Juventus have tied academy forward Destiny Elimoghale to the club until 30 June 2029, on the day Giovanni Carnevali spoke to shareholders about the youth sector. The 2009-born striker has already been named in a European squad while injuries stretch the first team.

The club confirmed Elimoghale’s renewal on 3 November. That was the same day chief executive Giovanni Carnevali addressed shareholders at the Allianz Stadium. He called for a single project covering the first team, the Next Gen and the youth sector.

Elimoghale has come through every level of the club’s academy. He has been at Juventus since childhood. This season he began playing professional football in Serie C.

The NEC fixture was the opening matchday of the Europa League league phase. Spalletti named three Next Gen players because the first team was hit by injuries, Tuttosport reported. Pagnucco and Owusu joined Elimoghale. All three were in a European squad for the first time.

It has been revealed that elimoghale did not get on the pitch in the comfortable win. He stayed on the bench as an unused substitute, alongside Vicario, Pinsoglio and Pagnucco.

Industry observers note that back in Serie C, his minutes have been mixed. In a 5-3 home defeat to Albinoleffe on the sixth matchday, he tried two long-range shots. One went just wide. Goalkeeper Baldi saved the other. At Trento on the 11th matchday, he replaced Leone in the 70th minute of a 2-1 defeat. The match came in Serie C Group A. He was among Massimo Brambilla’s unused substitutes in the 1-1 home draw with Pro Vercelli on 2 November. That matchday 12 fixture was the Next Gen’s most recent game.

Sources indicate that carnevali noted the club must bring its youth sector back to the level of recent years. He added that Juventus must keep trying to improve it. Securing a home-grown forward for the long term is consistent with that message.

Carnevali confirmed a change to the UEFA squad list as well, with Ekhator replacing Locatelli.

Aggiornamento della lista UEFA: Jeff Ekhator subentra a Manuel Locatelli. pic.twitter.com/I3Mi1W0PSB.

— JuventusFC (@juventusfc) November 3, 2026.

Recent findings suggest that for Elimoghale, the wider picture is a first team still short of bodies. Coaches have already turned to the Next Gen once in Europe. A new long-term deal means the club has secured one of those options.

Sources indicate that the squad remains stretched heading into the next round of European fixtures. McKennie is suffering from muscle fatigue and will miss the Europa League trip to AZ Alkmaar. Alajbegovic and Cabal are expected to be available in the Netherlands. The trip comes with the European squad list already being reshaped.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Everton could look to make a major statement in the January transfer window as David Moyes considers ways to strengthen his side’s attacking options.
  • After concerns over the team’s lack of goals, the Toffees are reportedly exploring a move for a forward with proven Premier League experience.
  • Manchester United’s Marcus Rashford has emerged as a potential target, with reports suggesting Everton are discussing the possibility of bringing the England international to Merseyside.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Everton could look to make a major statement in the January transfer window as David Moyes considers ways to strengthen his side’s attacking options.

After concerns over the team’s lack of goals, the Toffees are reportedly exploring a move for a forward with proven Premier League experience.

Manchester United’s Marcus Rashford has emerged as a potential target, with reports suggesting Everton are discussing the possibility of bringing the England international to Merseyside.

A deal would give Moyes another versatile attacking option, although several key details would need to be resolved before a transfer could progress.

According to Football Insider, former Everton chief executive Keith Wyness believes a move for Rashford is being discussed seriously ahead of the January window.

Industry observers note that speaking on Football Insider’s Inside Track podcast, Wyness stated: “Yes, this is definitely being talked about and quite strongly. And I think that could be an interesting solution.”.

The former Everton chief executive also pointed to Rashford’s previous loan spells and suggested that a move closer to Manchester could benefit the player.

In a recent development, “Rashford did well when he was on loan at Villa and at Barcelona as well. I think it could work, and I think being close to where he is in Manchester, just along the M63, could also benefit him greatly as well,” Wyness explained.

Sources indicate that the comments suggest that a January switch is a possibility worth monitoring, although neither club has confirmed an agreement. Separate reporting from FootballTransfers has also indicated that Everton and Manchester United have held early discussions over a potential winter move.

Industry observers note that wyness drew comparisons with Jack Grealish, who has made an impact at Everton when available, adding: “We’ve seen Jack (Grealish) moving across that way as well, and when he’s fit, Jack is certainly a major asset for Everton. So I think Rashford would be a very interesting signing, and I’m hearing there’s a lot of smoke here; it’s definitely being discussed.”.

He then added: “I wouldn’t be surprised to see something happening in January.”.

For Everton, Rashford’s versatility could be a major attraction. Although he has often operated from the left, he can also play centrally, potentially giving Moyes additional options across the frontline. His arrival could provide support for Thierno Barry and help address the team’s need for more goals.

However, the financial structure of any deal would be important. Everton would need to consider Rashford’s wages, Manchester United’s valuation and whether a permanent transfer or loan arrangement would be realistic. The forward’s willingness to join another Premier League club would also be a significant factor.

Recent findings suggest that rashford could represent an ambitious addition for Everton if the club can find an agreement that works financially. His Premier League experience and ability to operate in several attacking positions would give Moyes greater flexibility, while a change of environment could offer the player a fresh start.

The comparison with Grealish is particularly relevant to Everton’s approach. The club could look to provide Rashford with an environment in which he can rebuild his confidence and contribute more consistently, although any potential success would depend on his fitness, form and role within the team.

Nevertheless, a transfer is far from guaranteed. The reported discussions remain at an early stage, and Everton must still resolve the financial details and establish whether Rashford would be open to the move.

For now, Wyness’s comments add weight to speculation surrounding Everton’s January aims. If negotiations progress, Rashford could become a name to watch as Moyes looks to strengthen his attacking options for the second half of the season.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Chelsea could make another major investment in their attacking options as they assess potential additions ahead of the January transfer window.

With the Blues continuing to build a squad capable of competing for major honours, Barcelona midfielder Fermín López has reportedly emerged as a player of interest.

The 23-year-old Spain international has attracted attention from several European clubs, with Paris Saint-Germain also considering a move.

Chelsea previously attempted to sign López in 2025, and fresh reports suggest the London club could revisit their interest if the opportunity arises.

According to CaughtOffside, Chelsea and PSG are both prepared to make significant offers for López, who remains an important part of Barcelona’s aims under Hansi Flick.

A source with links to the agents industry told CaughtOffside: “PSG are preparing a serious offer worth around €80million for Fermin Lopez,” before adding: “Chelsea are also considering a massive bid.”.

In a recent development, the reported interest could set up a transfer battle between the Premier League side and the French champions. However, neither club has confirmed a formal bid, and any deal would depend on Barcelona’s position and the player’s willingness to leave his boyhood club.

According to recent reports, chelsea are familiar with López, having reportedly made a significant offer for him in the summer of 2025. The midfielder opted to remain at Barcelona, but the latest reports suggest the Blues could be willing to return if his circumstances change.

It has been revealed that lópez’s ability to operate as an attacking midfielder, contribute goals and create chances makes him an appealing option. His performances have also strengthened his reputation as a versatile attacking talent capable of influencing games from advanced positions.

In a recent development, competition for places at Barcelona could be one factor to monitor, although there is no confirmation that López is actively seeking an exit. CaughtOffside reports that Chelsea and PSG currently have the most concrete interest, while Arsenal and Manchester United have also made enquiries about his situation.

Sources indicate that barcelona, meanwhile, would reportedly prefer to retain the midfielder but could face pressure to consider substantial offers amid their financial challenges. López signed a contract extension in February 2026, keeping him at the club until 2031, meaning negotiations would likely require a significant financial commitment.

Recent findings suggest that chelsea may also have other priorities for January. The report identifies Bournemouth midfielder Alex Scott as a potential focus for the Blues, meaning any pursuit of López could depend on how their wider transfer plans develop.

#37347. Observation of tunable superradiant frequency combs

Observation of tunable superradiant frequency combs

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 17 min read (3428 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nature

⏱️ ~17 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Cavity quantum electrodynamics1 with quantum emitters coupled to resonators provides a powerful platform for engineering light–matter interactions2,3 and exploring many-body phenomena4,5.
  • This is a preview of subscription content, access via your institution.
  • Access Nature and 54 other Nature Portfolio journals.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Cavity quantum electrodynamics1 with quantum emitters coupled to resonators provides a powerful platform for engineering light–matter interactions2,3 and exploring many-body phenomena4,5. In particular, superradiance6—arising from collective quantum interference among emitters—has been explored as a route to ultrastable continuous radiation7. However, engineering superradiance in the time domain to realize periodic pulsed sources or frequency combs remains largely unexplored. Here we investigate the non-equilibrium many-body dynamics of a driven spin ensemble coupled with an on-chip superconducting resonator and uncover a dynamical phase transition from continuous-wave to periodic pulsed superradiant emission. To quantitatively capture the observed dynamical phases, we introduce a driven-dissipative cavity-quantum electrodynamics model that elucidates how the periodic pulsed superradiant phase emerges from collective, periodically repeating spin dynamics stabilized by the interplay of coherence growth, disorder and dissipation. We also find that rare-earth ion spin systems with both optical and microwave transitions enable phase-synchronized, dual-rail superradiant frequency combs in both the microwave and the optical domains. Our results not only open upcoming opportunities for atom-based frequency-comb sources and programmable superradiant generation, but establish a fundamental connection between periodic pulsed superradiance and the emergence of a continuous time crystal8,9,10 as a new non-equilibrium phase in driven open systems.

a, Detailed device schematic. A niobium film is patterned on a 500 μm thick 171Yb3+:YVO4 crystal. A 100 nm gold layer is evaporated on the back side, forming a weak optical Fabry-Pérot mode between the front and back chip reflections. b, Calibration of spin-cavity coupling strength. By optically pumping the population into the \(| \downarrow \rangle \) state, we probe the resonant spin-cavity coupling spectrum and its strength while avoiding superradiant effects. The blue data in the bottom subpanel correspond to the continuous-wave (CW) pump being off, while the black data are taken with a 400 μW continuous-wave pump. By fitting to a spin-cavity coupling model, we extract an ensemble coupling strength of \(\sqrt{N}g\approx 2\pi \times 1.1\) MHz, corresponding to a normalized coupling gnorm ≈ 0.6 < 1. The single-spin coupling, g = 2π × 10 Hz, and the effective ensemble size, N = 1010, are estimated from Comsol simulation and dopant concentration. c, Ensemble coupling strength, \(\sqrt{N}g\), as a function of pump power. We observe that the ensemble coupling strength increases with pump power, indicating a larger population in the microwave spin manifold.

Recent findings suggest that a, A pulsed, transient optical pumping scheme that drives 171Yb3+ spins into the \(| \uparrow \rangle \) state. The resulting inverted spin polarization is resonantly coupled to a microwave cavity, leading to a superradiant burst in the microwave domain. b, Example of a delayed superradiant burst. A 1 mW pump is applied for 50 μs, after which a microwave superradiant burst is observed with a delay time τd. The superradiant signal is normalized by its peak-to-peak amplitude. c and d, Burst delay times, τd, and burst width, τw, measured as a function of the optical pump detuning, Δpump, which controls the optical transition strength from \(| g\rangle \) to \(| \uparrow \rangle \). A symmetric dependence of τd and τw is observed, with shorter delay times and narrower widths near resonance. This behaviour is consistent with the expected scaling τd, τw ∝ 1/N, as the pump detuning effectively controls the ensemble size, N, in the microwave spin manifold. Data points represent mean values, with error bars indicating the standard deviation over 300 repeated measurements.

a, Frequency-domain measurement of continuous-wave microwave superradiance, showing a much narrow linewidth of  ≈ 30 Hz. The inhomogeneously broadened ensemble line profile (dashed line) is overlaid for comparison. b, Dependence of the linewidth of continuous-wave superradiance on emission power, PMW. An inverse relationship between the linewidth and the emission power is observed, consistent with a noise-broadened Schawlow-Townes linewidth. The lower dashed line denotes the pump laser noise-limited bound. These results confirm that the disordered spin ensemble emits continuous-wave superradiance with a much narrower spectral linewidth. c, Continuous-wave superradiance emission frequency at different optical pump detunings. A linear correlation between the microwave emission frequency and optical pump detuning is observed, with a slope of  −1.23 kHz/MHz.

a, Four representative data traces under a 1 ms continuous optical pump. Random onset times of the emergent periodic pulsed phase are observed. b, Zoom-in of individual burst trains showing the distribution of burst onset times, {τk}, where k denotes the experimental repetition index. After an initial settling time, both the amplitudes, {Ak}, and the periodicity, T, become independent of k, indicating the establishment of a robust pulsed superradiance phase. c, Burst onset phases, defined as θk = 2π × τk/T (mod 2π), measured over 50 repetitions under identical experimental conditions. The phases are randomly distributed over 2π, demonstrating spontaneous breaking of continuous time-translation symmetry in the absence of any external timing reference.

a, Schematic of periodic pulsed superradiance, characterized by three parameters: the pulse-train periodicity T, the peak emission power Ppeak, and the average emission power \({\overline{P}}_{{\rm{MW}}}\). b-d, show fits to the experimental data presented in Fig. 3 of the main text, where T, Ppeak, and \({\overline{P}}_{{\rm{MW}}}\) exhibit good agreement with the expected scaling behaviours of T ∝ 1/N, Ppeak ∝ N2, and \({\overline{P}}_{{\rm{MW}}}\propto {N}^{2}\), respectively. Here, N is the effective number of spins in the microwave manifold, tuned via the optical pump detuning, Δpump. When sweeping Δpump, the optical pump power is fixed, corresponding to an excitation over an optical inhomogeneity Γop = 2π × 92 MHz in all three cases.

a, Relative contributions of superradiance (blue) and stimulated emission (red) to the emission strength in the periodic superradiance phase. b, Comparison of emission patterns between the many-body case with N = 1010 atoms (blue) and the single-atom case with N = 1 (red). For a fair comparison, the total effective cavity coupling strength is fixed to \({g}_{{\rm{tot}}}=\sqrt{N}g=2\pi \times 1\,{\rm{MHz}}\) for both cases. c, Comparison of emission patterns in the presence (blue) and absence (red) of spin frequency inhomogeneity, i.e., disorder. All simulations are performed using experimental parameters corresponding to the periodic superradiance phase in Regime III.

In a recent development, a and b, show simultaneously recorded microwave periodic superradiance and transferred optical periodic superradiance, respectively, over a duration of up to 100 ms. c, Zoom-in windows near 1, 50, and 100 ms showing synchronized dual-rail emission patterns, maintaining persistent and robust pulse periodicity without decay.

a, Microwave (blue) and optical (yellow) amplitudes, A(t), extracted from IQ detection as A(t) = ∣I(t) + iQ(t)∣. The I and Q signals, I(t) and Q(t), are measured continuously over 2 ms, capturing 30 consecutive superradiant bursts. The microwave and optical channels exhibit synchronized and reproducible temporal profiles. The grey shaded area indicates the noise floor determined from the optical signal, below which the phase extraction is not reliable. b, Normalized amplitude stability over 30 consecutive superradiant bursts. τ denotes the peak emission time, identified for each burst from the time-domain pulse train. The error bars denote the standard deviations of the microwave and optical normalized amplitudes, which are 0.009 and 0.05, respectively. c, Time-domain phase profiles, \(\phi (t)={\tan }^{-1}[Q(t)/I(t)]\), extracted from IQ detection. The microwave and optical pulse trains exhibit synchronized and reproducible phase profiles over time. Phase values in regions dominated by the optical-signal noise floor are greyed out, where large fluctuations are observed. The chirping behaviour during each pulse qualitatively follows the amplitude profile, which can be attributed to an effective Kerr nonlinearity induced intensity dependence. d, Phase stability over 30 consecutive superradiant bursts, zoomed in on the region above the noise floor. The error bars denote the standard deviations of the microwave and optical phase values, which are 0.03π and 0.11π, respectively. See Methods for details.

  • David Moyes needs additional firepower to strengthen his squad, and a promising Iceland international has reportedly emerged as a potential solution.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Everton could make signing a new centre-forward a priority in January after entering the season short of options in attack.

David Moyes needs additional firepower to strengthen his squad, and a promising Iceland international has reportedly emerged as a potential solution.

Real Sociedad striker Orri Oskarsson is attracting interest from several Premier League clubs, with Everton understood to be paying particularly close attention to his progress.

The 22-year-old has impressed in Spain, and the Toffees could explore a move as they look to address a key weakness in their squad.

According to TEAMtalk, Everton are among the clubs monitoring Oskarsson ahead of the January transfer window. Tottenham Hotspur, Newcastle United, Sunderland and Brentford are also reportedly tracking the Icelandic forward, meaning Moyes could face competition if Everton decide to pursue a deal.

Sources indicate that everton’s need for a striker has become increasingly apparent following their summer business. Beto departed for Fiorentina without a replacement arriving, leaving Thierno Barry as the club’s only recognised centre-forward. Attempts to sign Folarin Balogun from Monaco and Joshua Zirkzee from Manchester United also failed to produce a deal.

That situation has reportedly encouraged Everton to examine their options ahead of January, with Oskarsson among the forwards attracting attention.

In a recent development, the Iceland international joined Real Sociedad from FC Copenhagen in 2024 and made progress during his previous campaign, scoring nine goals in LaLiga. His combination of physical presence, technical ability and finishing has helped establish him as an appealing prospect for clubs looking to strengthen their attacking ranks.

In a recent development, oskarsson has also continued to impress at international level, with his performances for Iceland adding to his growing reputation. At 22, he could offer Everton both an immediate option up front and a potential long-term investment.

It has been revealed that however, Everton would need to establish whether Real Sociedad are prepared to negotiate during the January window. The Spanish club invested significantly to secure his services, and there is no confirmation that they would be willing to let him leave midway through the season.

Oskarsson could be an important addition for Everton as Moyes looks to address the lack of depth at centre-forward. Relying heavily on Barry leaves the manager with limited specialist alternatives, particularly across a demanding second half of the campaign.

Industry observers note that the Icelandic striker’s profile could suit Everton’s need for another option capable of leading the line. His technical qualities may also give Moyes greater flexibility in how the team approaches matches, while his age offers scope for further development.

Recent findings suggest that competition from Tottenham, Newcastle, Sunderland and Brentford could complicate Everton’s pursuit, however. The Toffees would need to move decisively if their interest develops into a formal approach, while the final cost and Sociedad’s willingness to sell would be key factors.

For now, Everton’s reported interest suggests the club are assessing potential solutions ahead of January rather than confirming a deal is imminent. With Moyes needing greater depth in attack, Oskarsson is a name to watch as the winter transfer window approaches.

  • Both Racing de Santander and Real Sociedad will be aiming to make it back-to-back wins in Spain's top flight when they lock horns on Sunday afternoon.
  • Real Sociedad lead the overall head-to-head record between the two sides 49 wins to 34, while the Basque outfit have triumphed in the last three meetings.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Matt Law | 20 Nov 2026 20:16, Last updated: 20 Nov 2026 20:18.

Both Racing de Santander and Real Sociedad will be aiming to make it back-to-back wins in Spain's top flight when they lock horns on Sunday afternoon.

Real Sociedad lead the overall head-to-head record between the two sides 49 wins to 34, while the Basque outfit have triumphed in the last three meetings.

Racing have a record of four wins, two draws and six defeats from their 12 league matches this season, with 14 points leaving them in 10th spot in the La Liga table.

Jose Alberto's side entered the November international break off the back of a 2-1 victory over Malaga, and they have actually won three of their last four games in all competitions.

The Green and Whites are the reigning Segunda Division champions, securing a return to this level courtesy of their excellent second-tier campaign in 2025-26, and their main aim for this season will be to consolidate back in the top flight.

Racing have not managed to overcome Real Sociedad since March 2011, while they have just one victory over the Basque side since January 2007.

The Green and Whites have been impressive on home soil this season, picking up 11 points from their six matches in front of their own supporters.

Real Sociedad, meanwhile, boast a record of seven wins, one draw and four defeats from their 12 league matches this season, with 22 points leaving them fifth in the table.

The Basque outfit are only four points off fourth-placed Real Betis, and an excellent run of form in Spain's top flight has seen them win five of their last six matches.

La Real are also playing in the Europa League this season, picking up five points from their four matches to sit down in 20th position in the league stage.

Real Sociedad's last league match ended in a 1-0 win over Rayo Vallecano before the November international break, and they will have their eyes on another three points here before heading to England next week to tackle Crystal Palace in the Europa League.

Real Sociedad form (all competitions):.

Racing need to make late checks on Alvaro Mantilla and Andres Martin, but the hosts are otherwise in strong shape for their clash with Real Sociedad.

Yassir Zabiri has been in impressive form this season, scoring nine goals in 12 appearances, and the number 21 will continue through the middle for the hosts.

There is also expected to be a spot in the side for Ivan Martin.

As for Real Sociedad, Alvaro Odriozola remains unavailable for selection due to a knee injury, while Ander Barrenetxea is a major doubt due to a hamstring injury.

Mikel Oyarzabal missed the team's final match ahead of the November international break through illness, but the attacker has since returned for Spain, and it is possible that he could start in a wide area on Sunday due to the form of Orri Oskarsson.

The 22-year-old, who is being linked with a move to Manchester United, has scored four times in 10 league appearances this season, including the winner against Rayo Vallecano last time out, and he is again set to feature in the XI.

Agirrezabala; Ramon, Felipe, Belocian, Salinas; I Martin, Prati; Luque, Canales, Vicente; Zabiri.

Real Sociedad possible starting lineup:.

Remiro; Aramburu, Martin, Zubeldia, Munoz; Turrientes, Soler; Kubo, Sucic, Oyarzabal; Oskarsson.

Real Sociedad have lost three of their six away league matches this season, while Racing have been solid at home, so we are struggling to back a victory for the visitors and have instead settled on a low-scoring draw.

Harry Potter films turns 25 ahead of fresh TV series' release

💡 Key Takeaways

  • "Thousands of excited fans, some dressed up in wizard hats and cloaks, gathered to catch a glimpse of arriving celebrities," the BBC reported at the time.
  • Industry observers note that daniel Radcliffe, who played Harry Potter, was just 12 years old and clearly impressed by the spectacle.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that on November 4, 2001, London's Leicester Square became a world of witches and wizards. The occasion was the world premiere of "Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone" (released in the US and India as "Harry Potter and the Sorcerer's Stone").

"Thousands of excited fans, some dressed up in wizard hats and cloaks, gathered to catch a glimpse of arriving celebrities," the BBC reported at the time.

Industry observers note that daniel Radcliffe, who played Harry Potter, was just 12 years old and clearly impressed by the spectacle. The BBC quoted him as saying, "It is so cool. I have never heard my name shouted so much in an hour.".

The crowds highlighted just how far Harry Potter fever had spread in only four years.

The first Harry Potter book was published by Britain's Bloomsbury in June 1997, with an initial print run of just 500 hardcover copies.

About 5,000 paperback copies were also released around the same time.

Today, first editions are prized collectors' items, with hardcover copies commanding high prices at auction. In mid-October, one sold for $400,000 through US auction house Heritage Auctions.

At first, the book's popularity grew largely by word of mouth among schoolchildren. Media attention followed when it won the prestigious Nestle Smarties Book Prize later that year.

With an estimated 120 million-plus copies sold worldwide, it is the best-selling book in the series and ranks among the best-selling novels of all time.

Industry observers note that for years, J.K. Rowling's public image was defined by her extraordinary rise from a single mother on welfare to a billionaire.

But in recent years, debate over her views on gender and transgender identity has increasingly overshadowed that success. It's an issue Rowling herself frequently weighs in on.

In an essay published on her website on October 21, 2026, Rowling reiterated her opposition to what she calls the "current, dominant strain of trans activism." She argues that this movement "holds that a man who declares himself a woman is, literally, a woman, and is therefore entitled to be treated as a woman in all contexts." Rowling argues that allowing trans women into single-sex spaces poses a risk. She describes biological sex as an indisputable biological fact.

Such statements have led critics to accuse Rowling of transphobia, while others regard her stance as a defense of women's rights and safety.

The controversy has also divided her fans. Some stand by Rowling, while others try to draw a distinction between the books and their author.

It has been revealed that others have left Harry Potter behind altogether. One former fan is German YouTuber Coldmirror, known for her Harry Potter parodies. The media artist from the Bremen area, whose real name is Kathrin Fricke, told the Süddeutsche Zeitung newspaper: "I don't have any love left for Harry. I'm still somewhat interested, but I can no longer watch it in good conscience." She cited Rowling's campaigning against transgender people as the reason.

The "Harry Potter" film cast is divided as well. The three main stars — Daniel Radcliffe, Emma Watson and Rupert Grint — have publicly spoken out in support of transgender people. Meanwhile, Ralph Fiennes, who played Lord Voldemort, and Helena Bonham Carter, who portrayed Bellatrix Lestrange, have defended Rowling's right to express her views.

Sources indicate that despite the controversy surrounding Rowling, Warner Bros., which holds the Harry Potter film rights, is bringing the books back to the screen — this time as a series for HBO. The premiere is scheduled for December 25.

In a recent development, the eight-episode first season is an an adaption of the first book. Even though the episode lengths haven't been confirmed, the scope of a TV series gives each book much more room than the original films did. That means more time to explore subplots, character development and everyday life at Hogwarts. While many fans are looking forward to a more detailed adaptation, others remain skeptical. They find it hard to imagine the familiar characters being played by anyone else.

The newly introduced trio consists of Dominic McLaughlin as Harry Potter, Arabella Stanton as Hermione Granger and Alastair Stout as Ron Weasley.

Industry observers note that J.K. Rowling is an executive producer on the show. HBO notes, however, that her views on gender identity won't be reflected in the storyline. Several people involved in the latest production have publicly distanced themselves from her views. Paapa Essiedu, who has been cast as Severus Snape, signed an open letter supporting transgender people. Rowling subsequently remarked she had neither the power nor the desire to have him removed from the show because of it. John Lithgow, who plays Dumbledore, and Nick Frost, who portrays Hagrid, have also spoken out against Rowling's views.

Meanwhile, the Harry Potter merchandising machine is still going strong. On November 4, Britain's largest Harry Potter store to date is set to open in London. According to Warner Bros., the two-story shop covers more than 1,950 square meters.

  • Part of the money is already committed.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, juventus shareholders have cleared a capital increase of up to €250m, and majority owner Exor has already committed €60m of it. Giovanni Carnevali warned that the UEFA settlement means nothing extraordinary should be expected in January.

Juventus shareholders gave the board the power to raise up to €250m in new capital at the Allianz Stadium on 3 November. The vote came in the extraordinary part of the meeting and passed with 99.9% in favour. The same assembly approved the 2025/26 accounts.

Part of the money is already committed. Exor has already paid in €60m as an advance towards the capital increase. That payment supports the club’s equity and finances until the board uses its fresh authority. The majority owner has also guaranteed its own 65.4% stake in the raise and any shares other investors leave untaken.

The squad will not see the full sum. Shoring up the club’s finances across this season and next will take 45–50% of whatever is raised, according to Football Italia. That leaves roughly €100m mainly for first-team signings before the January window. Beyond keeping equity at a suitable level, the rest will go on controlling debt and keeping the team competitive, including transfers, Corriere dello Sport reports.

The accounts show why the balance sheet needs support. The consolidated loss for 2025/26 was €66.0m. That was €7.9m bigger than the previous year’s €58.1m. The result was in line with the forecasts in the club’s half-year report to 31 December 2025. The board had approved the accounts on 29 September. Another loss is expected in 2026/27, mainly because Juventus are in the Europa League rather than the Champions League.

Industry observers note that the assembly was Giovanni Carnevali’s first as chief executive. He promised a serious approach to the January window. His warning was just as clear. As a serious manufacturer, Juventus must honour its settlement agreement with UEFA and does not expect to do anything extraordinary.

Sources indicate that that agreement was declared on 30 June. It is a three-year settlement with the First Chamber of UEFA’s Club Financial Control Body. It relates to Juventus breaking UEFA’s Football Earnings Rule over the three seasons from 2022/23 to 2024/25.

For supporters, the message is mixed. The capital increase gives the club fresh resources. The settlement still dictates how quickly that money can be used on the pitch.

Shareholders also criticised the club for keeping a low profile in recent years. President Gianluca Ferrero declared Juventus open to dialogue with Tether.

The terms of the UEFA deal leave little margin. Missing the targets agreed with UEFA for the current season or the next two can lead to limits on the club’s UEFA List A and further sporting sanctions. The settlement runs until the 2027/28 financial year.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Adepoju Marvellous | 20 Nov 2026 20:54, Last updated: 20 Nov 2026 20:58.

A struggling Sparta Rotterdam outfit will set out in search of a return to winning ways in Sunday’s Eredivisie clash against AZ Alkmaar at Het Kasteel.

The visitors, meanwhile, travel to Rotterdam aiming for back-to-back wins for the first time since September, having snapped a three-game losing streak just before the international break.

AZ Alkmaar started the season with six wins and a draw from their opening seven Eredivisie matches, looking like the team to beat, but a 2-0 defeat to Feyenoord after the September break sparked a four-game winless run (D1, L3).

In arguably the game of the season so far, Leeroy Echteld’s men scored three times in the final 30 minutes of their most recent clash against Groningen to secure a 4-3 victory and keep themselves within three points of PSV Eindhoven at the top of the Eredivisie table.

De Kaasboeren have failed to win any of their league matches immediately preceding a Europa League group-stage fixture so far, and with a trip to Sparta Prague to follow this weekend, they will be eager to buck that trend of faltering domestically before continental duties.

AZ won both league meetings with Sparta last season, making it four wins from the last six encounters (D1, L1). Sunday’s visitors are also unbeaten in their last six trips to Het Kasteel, averaging two goals per game in that stretch.

However, AZ have struggled away from home recently, collecting just one point from the last nine available on their travels, which came in a 2-2 draw at Cambuur courtesy of a Mexx Merdink penalty seven minutes from time.

While not their heaviest, Sparta’s 3-1 defeat to newly-promoted ADO Den Haag was arguably their most disappointing loss of the 2026-27 season so far, especially given the momentum they carried into the clash after a thrilling 3-2 triumph over Groningen.

Rogier Meijer has now lost more than half of his 13 matches since taking charge in July, and pressure is beginning to mount on the 45-year-old.

Nevertheless, his experience at this level - having recently surpassed 200 matches as a manager in Dutch football - suggests he will be given time to turn things around.

Starting this weekend’s clash just two points clear of the drop zone, De Rood-Witte Gladiatoren risk ending matchday 13 inside the relegation places - a significant fall from grace for a side tipped to compete for Europe at the start of the campaign.

Only Utrecht and Willem II have conceded more goals than Sparta’s 29, and they are also one of five teams without a clean sheet, leaving little mystery about their biggest shortcoming this season.

Averaging 1.8 goals per game so far, Sunday’s hosts have fared reasonably well in attack, but an overreliance on Milan Zonneveld, who has been directly involved in nine of their 21 goals, can sometimes prove detrimental.

Goalkeeper Michael Brouwer is Sparta’s only injury concern for Sunday’s clash after he was forced off late in the defeat to ADO Den Haag.

Filip Bednarek replaced Brouwer off the bench last time out and is ready to deputise in goal again if required.

Lushendry Martes will need to keep his discipline in check, having already collected four yellow cards this season, as one more would trigger a one-match suspension.

Jizz Hornkamp has made just three appearances this season and remains unavailable for AZ, as do fellow Dutchmen Stije Resink and Jeroen Zoet, who are both yet to feature in 2026-27.

Lewis Schouten’s involvement this weekend is at the moment in doubt after he was absent from the win over Groningen.

Twenty-three-year-old Mexx Meerdink has six goals and an assist in his last seven club matches and will be expected to deliver once again.

Sparta Rotterdam possible starting lineup:.

Bednarek; Martes, Young, Verschuren, Martins Indi, Kuipers; Van Bergen, Quintero, Hatenboer, Babadi; Zonneveld.

AZ Alkmaar possible starting lineup:.

Gold for the West Bank: Meet Palestinian karate champ Mariam Bsharat

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, "After the referee lifted my hand to show I'm now a two-time world champion, it was a very overwhelming feeling," Mariam Bsharat said.
  • Recent findings suggest that themes of relief, joy and sacrifice are commonplace in the reflections of athletes after a big win.
  • "It was everyday life, seeing people get killed around me and houses getting bombed," she told DW of her upbringing in the occupied West Bank.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, "After the referee lifted my hand to show I'm now a two-time world champion, it was a very overwhelming feeling," Mariam Bsharat said. "Making history once is something, but making it twice is really something else. I felt very happy and I felt a big relief. Only I know how many sacrifices I made and how many hardships I needed to overcome.".

Recent findings suggest that themes of relief, joy and sacrifice are commonplace in the reflections of athletes after a big win. In Mariam Bsharat's case, it's about more than just dedication to training and taking care of the body. The 17-year-old won her second under-21 World Karate Championship gold medal competing for the Palestine national team in Poland in October.

"It was everyday life, seeing people get killed around me and houses getting bombed," she told DW of her upbringing in the occupied West Bank.

Sources indicate that "I faced challenges in transportation," Bsharat said. "I wasn't able to go from one city to another to be able to train with other people, so that I can actually prepare for competitions. I needed to travel to other countries like Jordan or Egypt ... which was very hard for me. And, financially, the support wasn't really the support an elite athlete needed.".

Growing up in Nablus, Bsharat had a narrow path to the top. But initially, it was her own reluctance that threatened to stop a champion career before it started.

"When I was a little kid, I did not really love it," remarked Bsharat, who competes in the division for fighters who weigh under 66 kilograms (145 pounds).

Sources indicate that "I started it because my family was in that sport," Bsharat said. "My father had a dojo, and my mother also did that sport. My siblings and my aunts and my uncles — it's a family thing. I started it because they were all doing it. In time, I started getting into it.".

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

In a recent development, family has been a constant source of comfort and inspiration for Bsharat. Her father and uncle have acted as manager and coach respectively. While her mother and siblings moved with Mariam to Hamburg, Germany, last year, her father remained in order to take care of his business, the dojo, though he visits and tries to be with his daughter in competitions. Integration has been made easier by her mastery of the language, taught to her by her German mother.

Bsharat has mixed feelings about leaving her homeland.

Recent findings suggest that "I'm thankful to be here because being in Germany opened lot of doors for me, and I think I have a brighter future here," Bsharat stated. "But also being in Palestine was just my everyday life, and I loved it there. My family was around me, my friends were around me, and I just felt comfortable, which was a big change coming here to Germany. I think every change comes with hardships.".

It has been revealed that as well as the obvious difficulties of living in an area occupied by Israel, there are particular challenges for sportspeople living in the West Bank and the Gaza Strip, with access to facilities, travel and constant security fears among them. As such, very few people from the Palestinian territories become successful on the international sporting stage. That, Bsharat noted, gives her responsibilities that are unusual and heavy for a person of any age, let alone a 17-year-old.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

According to recent reports, "Being an elite athlete in Palestine is something very special because not everybody in Palestine has that opportunity. There aren't really a lot of athletes that are elite and who win international medals,” Bsharat mentioned.

"So all that pressure from all the country and all the people, the family, the coaches are on me because I'm representing them, raising their flag,” she said. "I sometimes even forget to fight for myself and actually think about myself.".

It has been revealed that that has not yet proved a barrier to Bsharat, who is is ranked first in the world in her category by the World Karate Federation (WKF). With Palestine recognized by the International Olympic Committee, Bsharat would likely have been a contender to raise that flag in Los Angeles at the 2028 Olympics. But the sport was dropped from the Games in 2024.

"The global karate community remains steadfast in our belief that the natural place for karate is within the Olympic Games, and we sincerely hope that the incongruence we suffered in Paris 2024 and LA 2028 will be corrected for Brisbane 2032, if not sooner," the WKF wrote in response to the decision in 2024. The sport was also taken off the slate for the recent Youth Games in Senegal.

In a recent development, should karate return in Brisbane, Bsharat would likely be approaching her prime. In the meantime, she is looking forward to starting her journey as a senior when she turns 18. But she won't be hanging around.

"My goal is it to be a world champion at seniors, which is the hardest and the best thing you can achieve in karate," she said.

"But winning an Olympic medal, being called Olympic champion or just representing my country with that flag [is a thought that] is just full of happiness and pride.".

The interview was conducted by Janek Speight.

Pierre Sage has admitted that he fears for his future at Crystal Palace, adding that he felt “shame” after his side slumped to their joint-heaviest defeat by rivals Brighton and Hove Albion.

Recent findings suggest that sage replaced Oliver Glasner as manager in June but since then Palace have won just two league matches with him in at the helm. The south London club have taken seven points from seven Premier League games and have already conceded 17 goals, the most of any team in the league.

Recent findings suggest that “I don’t know,” Sage stated when asked if he will get enough time to rectify Palace’s slump. He admitted that his shame was about how Palace were overwhelmed, leaking three goals within the first nine minutes of the game before eventually losing 5-0.

“We are not at the level we expected, and I’m really sorry for that,” the 47-year-old remarked. “I just want to apologise to the fans because it’s not normal to show this face.”.

The Frenchman mentioned that he took full responsibility for the 5-0 defeat, and understood why hundreds of Palace fans left well before the final whistle.

“I cannot blame anybody because we didn’t do the job in a good way,” he said. “I’m responsible for this team, and when the team play as today, it’s not normal. It’s my fault. I understand them.

“Another feeling is about shame because that’s my feeling after the game and from the beginning. It’s not normal to not respect the necessary of this kind of game.”.

Sage admitted that he will be assessing how Palace need to rethink their approach in the coming fixtures, beginning with Thursday’s trip to Besiktas in the Europa League.

“The first work to do is on me,” he mentioned. “I’m responsible for what’s happened on the pitch, and I have a lot of work to do because I have to change this kind of thing.

Industry observers note that “It’s maybe in the preparation, in the way we give them the motivation to start the game just before in the locker room in the warm-up. We have to analyse that because it’s not normal. And today it was really at the highest level we cannot expect, and that’s the moment to change the thing.”.

For all the scrutiny on his back three, Sage urged his entire side to take greater defensive responsibility, highlighting how the team were too passive in pressing Brighton. Palace have struggled to regain the solidity that long characterised the side since the departures of Marc Guéhi in January and Maxence Lacroix this summer.

Industry observers note that “The way of defending is not only on the back three; it is for every player, and there are some things to do collectively, too,” Sage stated. “When we defend low we struggle a lot.”.

According to recent reports, sage joined Palace after a fine campaign with Lens. He led the club to second place in Ligue 1, just six points off Paris St-Germain, and victory in the Coupe de France. Yet, despite Sage’s reputation when he moved to Selhurst Park, his suitability for the Palace job is increasingly being questioned.

Three years ago, Patrick Vieira lost his job after a defeat by Brighton. Now, Sage could suffer the same fate, with doubts growing that he will still be in charge for Thursday’s trip to Besiktas.

According to recent reports, “It’s not my decision,” Sage said. “I don’t want to accept the level of the moment if we are able to do better. And today the work is really important to do, and I will do it. It’s my job, and I’d like to change this.”.

With only Manchester City and Arsenal above them, Brighton and Hove Albion are entitled to dream of making history. Yet, whatever happens between now and May, one accolade is already surely their own: the goal of the season award.

Diego Gómez’s 56-yard strike will instantly become the stuff of Brighton lore. The Paraguayan’s audacity will be even more cherished for coming against Crystal Palace, who were pummelled 5-0 in the M23 derby.

In a recent development, good afternoon and welcome to our live coverage of the M23 derby – or El Gatwicko, as the kids call it these days – as high-flying Brighton and Hove Albion host Crystal Palace at the Amex Stadium. Being frank, this is neither the fiercest nor the most storied Premier League rivalry, but few would have imagined when these sides faced off in the Third Division in the mid-1970s that this would ever become a top-flight match-up sandwiched between European games.

Sources indicate that brighton have been outstanding this season and took their league form into the Conference League, thrashing Lithuanian champions Kauno Zalgiris on Thursday night. Fabian Hürzeler was delighted by his fringe players’ performances on Thursday night and may have some selection questions to answer with Jack Hinshelwood and Georginio Rutter finding the net. Brighton are third in the Premier League and were the division’s heaviest scorers after the last round of matches.

Yet the Palace nut has been a tough one to crack for Hürzeler, having not yet registered a win in four attempts. When asked what he enjoyed most about the rivalry, the German said: “Nothing yet, because I didn’t win any games so far. Hopefully on Sunday this changes… I like these games because they’re derbies, more emotions, it’s a rivalry, it’s [us] against Crystal Palace.”.

It has been revealed that in his pre-match interview Hürzeler admitted to being an admirer of Pierre Sage, and while the Frenchman’s side have failed to match Brighton’s fast start, they rallied impressively to defeat rivals Nottingham Forest last weekend and fought back valiantly away at Lyon, albeit in a losing effort, in midweek. Nico Paz compared to Messi and Maradona amid Real Madrid return rumours

💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Naim Beneddra | 20 Nov 2026 20:57, Last updated: 20 Nov 2026 21:01.
  • Real Madrid's reported prepares to bring Nico Paz back to the Santiago Bernabeu for £68m have attracted fresh attention after former Manchester United and Chelsea midfielder Juan Sebastian Veron compared the Argentine youngster's abilities to those of Lionel Messi and Diego Maradona.
  • Los Blancos are reportedly preparing to activate their €80m (£68m) buy-back option for the Como playmaker next summer, having watched his remarkable development under Cesc Fabregas in Serie A.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Naim Beneddra | 20 Nov 2026 20:57, Last updated: 20 Nov 2026 21:01.

Real Madrid's reported prepares to bring Nico Paz back to the Santiago Bernabeu for £68m have attracted fresh attention after former Manchester United and Chelsea midfielder Juan Sebastian Veron compared the Argentine youngster's abilities to those of Lionel Messi and Diego Maradona.

Los Blancos are reportedly preparing to activate their €80m (£68m) buy-back option for the Como playmaker next summer, having watched his remarkable development under Cesc Fabregas in Serie A.

According to Spanish radio station COPE, Madrid have decided to exercise the clause, which can only be triggered during the summer 2027 transfer window.

The 22-year-old has scored six goals and provided eight assists in 14 club appearances this season, establishing himself as one of the most influential attacking midfielders in Italian football.

However, Veron's latest assessment of Paz offers more than an extraordinary comparison with two of Argentina's greatest players.

The former Argentina international has also emphasised the importance of regular football in developing young talents, a consideration that could become significant if Paz returns to a Madrid squad already containing Jude Bellingham and Arda Guler.

Speaking in an interview with La Gazzetta dello Sport, Veron reserved exceptional praise for Paz after the midfielder continued his impressive international development.

"Nico Paz has incredible talent. He is destined for great things," the former Manchester United midfielder remarked. "The future belongs to him if he continues to behave like a professional, as he is doing.".

Sources indicate that veron then made a particularly striking comparison. "At 22, I have only seen Messi and a certain Diego Armando Maradona do certain things like that.".

Recent findings suggest that the 51-year-old was careful not to suggest that Paz was guaranteed to reach the extraordinary heights achieved by either legend. "I don't mean that he will reach those levels, but he has the qualities to attempt it," Veron explained.

What particularly impresses the former Chelsea midfielder is the confidence Paz displays when receiving possession under pressure.

Veron highlighted the youngster's ability to dictate the rhythm of attacks, move into dangerous positions and retain the trust of his teammates even when closely marked.

Rather than describing him solely as an individual talent, he identified Paz as the player around whom Como organise much of their attacking football.

"Nico is a leader in the way he manages moves. He is the focal point of the game," Veron added.

Those qualities have become increasingly apparent under Fabregas, whose possession-based approach has allowed the Argentine to develop into a central figure.

Sources indicate that paz has also carried his club form onto the international stage. He recently scored twice for Argentina against Costa Rica, further strengthening his credentials as one of the country's leading young talents following Messi's international retirement.

His performances have inevitably increased speculation surrounding his next move, with Madrid retaining a significant advantage over other potential suitors.

Paz left Madrid for Como in the summer of 2024, having made only eight senior appearances for the Spanish giants.

His move to Italy initially offered an opportunity to gain regular first-team experience, but the relationship between the two clubs has since become more complicated.

During the summer of 2026, Como reportedly paid an additional €60m to acquire full ownership of the player, while Madrid retained a final buy-back option worth €80m.

That clause is valid for the summer of 2027, meaning Madrid have a limited opportunity to bring their former academy player back on preferential terms.

COPE now reports that the Spanish giants intend to exercise that option, although the deal has not been officially completed.

As previously reported by Sports Mole, Madrid face an crucial decision over Paz's future, particularly because of the attacking competition awaiting him at the Bernabeu.

Bellingham has established himself as a key figure in Madrid's midfield, while Guler has also become increasingly influential under Jose Mourinho.

The club possesses several other attacking options, including Kylian Mbappe, Vinicius Junior and Yan Diomande. Consequently, there is no guarantee that Paz would enjoy the same importance in Madrid's starting XI that he presently possesses at Como.

Veron's comments about another young Argentine, Franco Mastantuono, offer an interesting perspective on that challenge.

Discussing the youngster's development during his loan spell at Fiorentina, Veron argued that consistent opportunities were essential for establishing himself at the highest level.

"Nico Paz became a leader at Como by playing," he explained. "I have never known a player who became a team leader by sitting on the bench.".

Veron was discussing the benefits of regular football rather than explicitly warning Paz against returning to Madrid. Nevertheless, his observations underline an notable consideration for the Spanish club as it weighs up the midfielder's future.

Paz reportedly chose to remain at Como last summer because he wanted to continue developing through regular appearances, and his decision has been rewarded by an outstanding start to the new campaign.

Manchester United have also been linked with the Argentina international, although Madrid's contractual advantage places the Spanish giants in a stronger position.

Industry observers note that for Los Blancos, securing a player whose value has risen considerably could represent an attractive investment. For Paz, the sporting challenge would be to turn the promise recognised by Veron into an influential role at a club where competition for attacking positions is already fierce.

By OLIVER HOLT, CHIEF SPORTS WRITER.

Published: 21:00 EST, 19 November 2026 | Updated: 22:15 EST, 19 November 2026.

Towards the end of the Australian summer of 2014-15, as the country prepared to host the Cricket World Cup, I took a flight from Sydney to Hobart, Tasmania, to watch a Sheffield Shield game between Tasmania and New South Wales at the Bellerive Oval, a beautiful ground perched on the banks of the Derwent River.

It has been revealed that australian sport was still in shock. A few months earlier, Australia's Test opener, Phillip Hughes, had died after he was struck on the side of his neck by a short ball from a young bowler called Sean Abbott in a game between Fresh South Wales and South Australia at the Sydney Cricket Ground.

In a recent development, hughes was treated at the ground for 40 minutes and then taken by ambulance to St Vincent's Hospital in nearby Darlinghurst in a critical condition. 'Feeling for Phil Hughes after being hit,' former Australia Test cricketer Dean Jones wrote on Twitter. 'He is not in a good way! Stay strong Sean Abbott. Not your fault, young man.'.

It has been revealed that the impact of the ball had compressed a vein in Hughes' neck and when it split, it caused a catastrophic bleed on the brain. Hughes had emergency surgery and was placed in an induced coma. He never regained consciousness and passed away two days later.

Industry observers note that hughes was a popular, talented, gutsy cricketer with three Test centuries already under his belt. A small guy with the heart of a lion. He was 25 years old. Cricket mourned a terrible tragedy – some called it the sport's saddest day and the agony of Hughes' family was hard to bear. But there was something else. There was an awareness that two tragedies were playing out in front of us.

Hughes was lost but the man who had bowled the delivery that felled him had been left behind, desolate and distraught. Many thought Sean Abbott, who was 22, would never play cricket again. That he would not be able to find the strength. But that was why I had flown to Tasmania. Because Abbott had found the strength.

Phil Hughes was the golden boy of Australian cricket in 2014, with three Test centuries already to his name, when he was hit by a ball bowled by Sean Abbott and died.

Abbott visiting the Sydney hospital where Hughes was in a coma that he would never wake from, having suffered a catastrophic bleed on the brain.

That February afternoon at the Bellerive Oval, I sat among a smattering of spectators who watched Abbott walk to the top of his mark. His team-mates shouted encouragement to him. They were willing him on with everything they had and Abbott bowled his heart out.

Industry observers note that 'Beautifully bowled, Abbo,' one of the NSW fielders shouted after one ball to former Test opener Ed Cowan. 'That's a beauty, Seanie,' another yelled after the fifth ball of his first over, when Cowan jerked his head out of the way of a short delivery so fast he fell over. Only one wicket fell that afternoon. Abbott took it.

It was one of the bravest sporting performances I have ever witnessed. Because even though cricket had voiced its support for Abbott, the sport could not protect him from his thoughts and from the knowledge he had become one of a cursed band of sportsmen who have unwittingly caused the death of an opponent during a contest.

Sources indicate that sometimes, tragedy in sport is not just the tragedy of the player who dies; it is the tragedy of the opponent who must live the nightmare of what he has done over and over again in his mind. To those that it has befallen, they say it is a grief that never leaves them.

In a recent development, that grief, that sense of a double tragedy, was brought sharply back into focus earlier this month when Tenerife striker Jesus de Miguel died in hospital the day after a sickening collision with FC Andorra goalkeeper Jesus Owono. The accident happened in the final minutes of a game in Spain's Segunda Division, when Owono hurtled out of his goal and collided with De Miguel in the centre circle. He was shown a red card for the foul.

In a recent development, there was an outpouring of grief for De Miguel. I was among those who observed a minute's silence for him before the Barcelona-Aston Villa Champions League tie at the Nou Camp the next evening. Tributes continue to be paid to him. Owono, meanwhile, has become a pariah. It is said that the 25-year-old rarely leaves his house.

It has been revealed that owono does not appear to have had the same sympathy extended to him that Abbott benefited from. His challenge on De Miguel, a striker who had had a peripatetic career in Spain's lower leagues, was reckless and cavalier. For him, the struggle with guilt and responsibility and public judgment is only just beginning.

FC Andorra will play their first home game since the tragedy against Leganes on Friday night but when they run out at the Encamp Stadium, a neat little ground beside a babbling river, the Valira d'Orient, and in the shadow of the mountains that make Andorra such a popular ski resort, Owono will not be there.

Earlier this month Tenerife striker Jesus de Miguel died in hospital the day after a sickening collision with FC Andorra goalkeeper Jesus Owono.

According to recent reports, owono has become a pariah. It is said that the 25-year-old rarely leaves his house.

Industry observers note that no one knows whether Owono will feel able to return to football when his ban ends. Footage circulated of him in an on-field argument moments before the clash with De Miguel, and it was used to suggest that he was in an unstable state of mind.

Some have pressed for him to be charged with manslaughter. His Instagram account was deactivated after it was deluged with abuse, including messages which branded him 'a murderer'. In a recent development, I spoke to the great British fighter Barry McGuigan about Owono this week. McGuigan has suffered his share of tragedies. His brother, Dermot, took his own life. According to recent reports, in the 12th fight of his professional career, McGuigan fought a Nigerian boxer called Young Ali at the World Sporting Club in Mayfair. He still remembers the clink of cutlery coming from the diners who were sitting ringside that night. That sound still takes him back.

According to recent reports, mcGuigan still remembers the sequence of punches that put Young Ali down in the sixth round of the fight. He saw his opponent's eyes roll back in his head and a feeling of dread washed over him. Young Ali, just 21, fell into a coma from which he never emerged and died five months later.

I spoke to the great British fighter Barry McGuigan (right) about Owono this week. McGuigan has suffered his share of tragedies.

According to recent reports, 'There was the horror of that and we sat and we waited and we prayed that he would be better and he never got better,' McGuigan told me. 'I didn't know whether I wanted to continue boxing. I thought: "If I can do this to somebody…"'.

According to recent reports, he shuddered when he talked about Owono. 'Other tragedies happen and other terrible things happen,' he stated. 'Life is a struggle. Something like that, you never leave it behind you.

According to recent reports, 'It is something invisible and it depends how emotionally vulnerable he is. He may never be the same again but I hope he is able to overcome it.'.

Recent findings suggest that there are others out there in sport, still trying to overcome it. Think of Matt Petgrave, the Sheffield Steelers ice-hockey player who was arrested on suspicion of manslaughter after his skate fatally cut the neck of Nottingham Panthers' Adam Johnson in an Elite Ice Hockey League match at Sheffield Arena in October 2023.

It has been revealed that think of Jochen Mass, the Formula One driver, who spent years blaming himself for the death of Gilles Villeneuve during qualifying for the Belgian Grand Prix at Zolder in 1982, because he slowed and moved to the right in front of Villeneuve. The Ferrari ran into the back of Mass and flipped in grotesque cartwheels across the track.

Think of Matthias Behr, the German fencer who killed his opponent, Vladimir Smirnov, at the 1982 World Fencing Championships in Rome when Behr's foil blade broke during a match, penetrated the Ukrainian fencer's mask and pierced his eye.

Think of Gary Cully, the Irish fighter, who learned this week that his last opponent, Lee Reeves, had died after spending three months in a coma following their bout in Dublin in August.

In a recent development, 'What a character and a gent,' Cully wrote in tribute to Reeves. 'It's never been nothing but love between us champ, can't really believe I'm writing this but RIP brother.'.

Nottingham Panthers' Adam Johnson died in October 2023 when opponent Matt Petgrave's skate cut his neck during a match.

Gary Cully (left), the Irish fighter, learned this week that his last opponent, Lee Reeves (right), had died after spending three months in a coma following their bout in Dublin in August.

Dr Victor Thompson, a prominent UK clinical sports psychologist, has studied the effect on competitors of being involved in the death of a rival.

Industry observers note that 'The biggest thing a player will have had to absorb normally is bad performance,' Dr Thompson claims. 'Now he has to absorb the fact that he was involved in somebody dying. He will be trying to work out was it his fault? Is he to blame? And all of that, because the emotions are so high, gets associated with playing the sport in question.

'So when Sean Abbott thought about going out there again, when he thought about putting his pads on, or putting his kit on and being around team-mates or the smell of the cricket bat – it'll all be associated to that very traumatic day.'.

According to recent reports, university of North Carolina academic John M Silva III argued that aggression in sport is defined in two categories: hostile aggression and instrumental aggression. Hostile is when the main aim is to cause harm or injury to your opponent. Instrumental is aggression for a purpose, perhaps ball recovery or to sow doubt in an opponent’s mind.

The interpretation of a player's actions at a time of high stress, frustration or adversarial combat is often central to the reaction to a sporting tragedy. Whether forgiveness is extended to or opprobrium visited on the competitor who has caused the death of another.

It has been revealed that that interpretation was used against Petgrave, who was notorious for having a bad disciplinary record on the ice. Some likened the action which fatally injured Johnson to a kung-fu kick and drew a link between it and some of his past behaviour. He was mercilessly trolled on social media. Team-mates, and many ice hockey fans, leapt to his defence and said any suggestion his action was deliberate was fanciful. They said his unusual action in lifting his left skate high was a direct result of being knocked off balance by a collision.

Petgrave could not return to ice hockey immediately even if he had wanted to. It was a full 18 months before the Crown Prosecution Service and South Yorkshire Police decided there was no realistic prospect of conviction for manslaughter and that no criminal charges should be brought against the 34-year-old Canadian.

It has been revealed that in the intervening period, Petgrave's family set up a crowdfunding page, pointing out that he was unable to work or to return home until the CPS had decided whether to press charges. The page raised nearly £20,000 from well-wishers.

The interpretation of a player's actions at a time of high stress, frustration or adversarial combat is often central to the reaction to a sporting tragedy - as it was for Petgrave.

Petgrave did receive widespread support from inside his sport, with a standing ovation at his Sheffield side's next home match, while he was beginning 18 months under investigation.

'This has been the most painful and overwhelming period of our lives,' a message from Petgrave's family said at the bottom of the page. 'Watching someone I love go through this has been incredibly difficult.

'Despite everything, we are doing our best to stay strong, and the support and kindness from so many people have been a source of strength. We continue to recognise the heartbreaking nature of this situation, and our thoughts remain with everyone affected. We hold on to hope that this will soon come to an end.'.

Sources indicate that petgrave now plies his trade in the minor league ECHL for the Indy Fuel, a team based in Fishers, Indiana. He is an ever-present this season, playing opponents like the Wheeling Nailers, the Greenville Swamp Rabbits, the Kalamazoo Wings and the Bloomington Bison.

According to recent reports, 'We understand the responsibility that comes with the great support we receive from this community,' Sean Hallett, CEO of Hallett Sports, which owns the Fuel, said when they hired Petgrave. 'We are confident he will be a positive addition to our team and our city.'.

I wrote to the Fuel, asking if there was any chance of speaking to Petgrave. They did not respond. The reticence is understandable and, in many ways, laudable. Players involved in this kind of tragedy are preoccupied with respect for the victims' families and the sensitivities that come with such terrible grief. There is nothing they can say or do to make it better.

Industry observers note that sometimes, it is the other way round. Sometimes, it is the family of a lost loved one who find a way to ease the pain of a sportsman eaten up by shame for inadvertently causing the death of a competitor.

Recent findings suggest that mass, who died last year, blamed himself for the sickening crash that killed the most exciting, charismatic, talented, electrifying driver in Formula One. As Villeneuve's Ferrari cartwheeled across the track, breaking into pieces, he was flung clear of the wreckage still strapped to his seat, catapulting across the track until he came to rest in the catch-fencing by the side of the circuit. He died of catastrophic injuries later that evening, aged 32.

Mass was absolved of responsibility. It was a tragic accident. Villeneuve was running hot after a disagreement with his team-mate Didier Pironi and was pushing even his own boundaries. There were any number of extenuating circumstances but Mass still blamed himself. He retired from the sport the same season.

As Gilles Villeneuve's Ferrari cartwheeled across the track, breaking into pieces, he was flung clear of the wreckage still strapped to his seat, catapulting across the track.

Despite being absolved of responsibility, Jochen Mass (pictured in 2019) blamed himself for the accident and retired from the sport the same year.

It was years later when he felt a tap on the shoulder as he was sitting on a plane. He looked up to see Villeneuve's son, Jacques, the 1997 F1 world champion, standing over him.

'I felt so guilty about what had happened and then suddenly, there was Jacques,' Mass recalled. 'He said: "Jochen, our family – we never blamed you. It was a racing incident – just a wrong decision by the two of you."'.

All the shame that Mass felt ebbed away. He found his own peace just as Behr found redemption by sheltering the grandchildren of Smirnov and his widow, Emma, at his home in Germany to protect them from the Russian invasion of Ukraine.

Behr, tortured by guilt about the accident that killed Smirnov, had written to Emma 30 years ago but the letter was lost. When he did not receive a reply, he was convinced that Smirnov's widow blamed him for killing her husband.

They finally met when a television documentary crew brought them together and Emma reassured Behr that she had never held him responsible. Behr has suffered from depression and suicidal thoughts because of flashbacks to the fatal accident.

'They are always there,' Behr said later. 'Even if I go into a liquor store and see vodka with the Smirnoff label on it, the thoughts of what happened immediately come back to me. But now that I am playing a part in the lives of Vladimir's grandchildren, it has come full circle for me. It was a gift for me. I can finally give something back.'.

Maybe Abbott has been trying to give something back all these years, too. Perhaps the fine career he has had is his tribute to Hughes. Many had worried that Abbott would not play again after Hughes' death. Not your fault, young man. Easy to say, harder to grasp amid the grief and the disbelief. But there was an outpouring of support for him, including from Hughes' family.

Perhaps the fine career 2023 World Cup winner Sean Abbott (bottom right) has had is his tribute to Hughes.

Sources indicate that that afternoon at the Bellerive Oval, I asked him about the day's play as he came off. He said he was happy with how it had gone. Afterwards, I sat in the stand with Abbott's team-mate Nathan Lyon, the Australia spinner, who spoke movingly about Hughes and about Abbott.
