Except it wasn't too easy. Inside, Lyon and the rest of Australian cricket were still in agony. Later that day, Lyon complained to Cricket Australia that he had not been expecting to be asked about Hughes. He was upset about my questions. I had made a misjudgment. Things were still too raw.

Sources indicate that lyon was comfortable talking about Abbott, though. 'The way Sean has carried himself through the whole incident, well, credit goes to him,' Lyon remarked. 'He is a very impressive bloke. I've got a lot of time for him. He will do anything to help anyone out. He always puts mates first. He always has your back. He is a typical good mate. I'm proud to call him a mate.

Industry observers note that 'I think (Abbott not playing again) went through the minds of a few of us. But natural instinct will come over and you do what you do best and if that's play cricket, you go out and play cricket. It's about being around your mates and the mates who are there with him now, they're the guys who are going to get him through it.'.

Sources indicate that abbott has never spoken about the tragedy. He gave written evidence in January 2016 to the inquest into Hughes' death.

'I saw him start to sway and I ran to the other end of the pitch and I held the right side of his head with my left hand,' Abbott wrote. Once in the changing room I felt confused and upset, I had a headache, people kept coming up to me but I cannot recall what they stated.'.

Much of the inquest was dominated by suggestions that Hughes had been subjected to a barrage of short balls and sledging. The inquest heard that Abbott's bowling partner, Doug Bollinger, had said to Hughes 'I'm going to kill you' at one stage during the game. Bollinger denied that accusation. Abbott was exonerated of any responsibility for the tragedy that unfolded.

According to recent reports, only rarely are there glimpses of the impact that Hughes' death has had on him. At a tribute to Hughes on the tenth anniversary of his death, Abbott broke down and wept at the end of the minute's silence at the SCG. One of his team-mates put an arm around his shoulders to try to comfort him.

Abbott at Hughes' funeral in his hometown of Macksville, Australia, in 2014.

Industry observers note that 'The difficulty with boxing is that you are in this sport to hurt your opponent,' states McGuigan. 'Nobody believes - or wants to believe - that it is going to do lasting damage'.

It has been revealed that mcGuigan notes the pain never quite goes away. 'I had a love-hate relationship with boxing,' he says. 'The difficulty with boxing is that you are in this sport to hurt your opponent. Nobody believes – or wants to believe – that it is going to do lasting damage.

What the Democrats' midterms win means for the US economy and Trump

📅 04 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1054 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • For the millions who cast their ballots in the US midterm elections, one concern ranked above all others: the economy.
  • So what does the Democrats' stunning capture of both the US Senate and House of Representatives mean for the economy and economic policy, given that President Donald Trump still has two years of his term to go?
  • According to recent reports, markets have rebounded after initially trending negatively.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

For the millions who cast their ballots in the US midterm elections, one concern ranked above all others: the economy.

So what does the Democrats' stunning capture of both the US Senate and House of Representatives mean for the economy and economic policy, given that President Donald Trump still has two years of his term to go?

According to recent reports, markets have rebounded after initially trending negatively. Global stocks rallied as investors appeared to take heart from the Democrats' victory.

With Democrats now holding comfortable majorities in both houses of Congress and Trump still in the White House, it could lead to gridlock in Washington. Trump has already said he would become "Mr Veto," meaning he would block any legislation the Democrats advance.

"The magnitude of the gains for the Democrats in the midterms does not change too much for the near-term policy outlook, given the party still lacks a filibuster-proof majority in the Senate and President Trump has veto power to block legislation," Stephen Brown, chief North America economist with Capital Economics, stated in a note.

Recent findings suggest that "I think we are looking at two years of complete 100% gridlock," Jacob Funk Kirkegaard, nonresident senior fellow with the Peterson Institute for International Economics, told DW after the results came in. "Nothing will get done of any kind.".

Some investors appear worried that the Democrats could force through AI regulation, especially if they also win the White House in 2028. Rising opposition among large majorities of the US population to data centers — the key infrastructure behind AI — helped secure victories for many Democratic candidates.

Kirkegaard, who is also a senior fellow at Bruegel, a European economics think tank, said the vote revealed the extent of that opposition. Even if the Democrats can't force regulation, he thinks local opposition will make it harder for data centers to be built, which could hit the valuation of significant tech firms that have benefitted from the AI boom.

"This election shows that the political underpinning of the rapid, aggressive AI growth story is shaky," he said. "It doesn't mean it's going to stop or be made illegal, but the dynamic of the growth story has shifted.".

If the Democrats were to win the presidency in 2028, Brown stated, they would be perfectly placed to make major policy changes. "That includes the potential for tax hikes on corporations and high-income individuals as well as regulation that could delay the AI rollout," he said.

According to polling conducted in early October by the Pew Research Center, 56% of Americans say Trump's tariff policies will have mostly negative impacts on the country, with only 20% saying mostly positive.

It has been revealed that that sentiment clearly drove many Democrats to victory in the midterms — particularly in states where tariffs have had a particularly negative impact. That includes those with sectors reliant on exports, such as Texas, Michigan, Iowa and Illinois, where counter-tariffs have hit and those that have high trade volumes with Canada.

Yet, barring an unprecedented climbdown from Trump — who has been ideologically wedded to tariffs since he first became a public figure almost 50 years ago — it's not clear how the Democrats could force substantial change to the president's signature economic policy.

"Trump will not be moderated," Deborah Elms, head of trade policy at the Hinrich Foundation in Singapore, told DW earlier this year. "Expect him to continue his trade disruption and tariff policies for as long as he remains in the Oval Office.".

Though the US Constitution gives Congress the power to collect and organize tariffs, various laws passed over the years have given presidents power to implement tariffs when they cite certain conditions, such as national security or economic emergencies.

Trump has already used such avenues for his tariffs and can continue to do so, despite some legal rebukes. However, while Congress can't necessarily force an end to Trump's existing tariffs, it can now take further legal action against them to prevent greater escalation.

Though Trump and the Democrats are clearly not going to make common cause, Kirkegaard mentioned, the scale of the Republicans' defeat might force Trump to be less erratic in his policymaking, from escalating his trade war with Canada to his Iran policy.

Trump remarked in the aftermath of Tuesday's defeats that he would "work with" the Democrats and told the Financial Times in the run-up to the vote that he was unlikely to escalate the war in Iran.

Were a deal to be struck with Iran, soaring energy prices — a pivotal election concern — could finally fall, helping voters with their cost-of-living concerns.

"You've got to get a deal with Iran, and you've got to bring down gas prices," Kirkegaard noted. "From a political point of view, that's the most important thing now.".

George Saravelos, an analyst with Deutsche Bank FX Research, thinks the markets are beginning to become more optimistic in that area. "With oil flows through the Middle East having materially recovered, the market is pricing a large imminent risk premium of re-escalation and energy supply disruption," he said in a note.

Despite the scale of the Democrats' victory, the fact that Trump remains in the Oval Office will complicate all efforts to force a change to signature economic policies and complications.

In a recent development, yet Congress can now exert considerable pressure. Another problem vital to voters was corruption and the belief that the Trump administration has engaged in corruption and personal enrichment while in office.

That raises the prospect of the fresh Democratic-controlled Congress launching legal investigations and potentially pursuing another impeachment of Trump, which could force the president to negotiate on some economic challenges to secure his political survival.

"Can you find 10 or 12 Republican senators who, in the face of overwhelming corruption, would be willing to vote for articles of impeachment? I wouldn't rule it out," Kirkegaard remarked. "And that's a scenario in which Trump might suddenly be much more accommodating to, for instance, abandoning most of his tariffs.".

Despite voters' clear rejection of Trump's economic policies, the Democratic Party's newly minted senators, congressmen and congresswomen face an uphill battle in trying to reverse them.

Arsenal, Liverpool and Chelsea have all contacted Bournemouth about England midfielder Alex Scott, according to CaughtOffside, which cites The i Paper. Liverpool and Chelsea want to move in January, while Arsenal would rather wait until next summer. Bournemouth’s stance on selling the 23-year-old has softened, but the reported asking price is above £100m, and Scott turned down two contract offers over the summer.

Recent findings suggest that the interest has clear reasons behind it. Andoni Iraola coached Scott at Bournemouth before taking over at Anfield in June, and Liverpool want to reunite them. Chelsea lost Enzo Fernandez to Manchester City in a £125m deadline-day deal and had a reported £64m bid for Scott rejected earlier in the summer. Scott wins the ball, presses and carries it through midfield, and he started Bournemouth’s first five league games this season before a quadriceps injury on England duty in October kept him out for weeks. Fitness is the first concern, because knee problems have interrupted much of his time on the south coast. End product is the second. He has scored five league goals in 85 appearances since joining in 2023, so he will not solve a shortage of chances alone.

In a recent development, not at £100m, and not as a January priority. Liverpool rank 18th for big chances after ten league games, according to This Is Anfield, and Scott offers energy rather than creativity. The real gap sits beside Ryan Gravenberch, where Curtis Jones left in the summer, and nobody arrived to share the defensive work.

Scott could be the aggressive partner in Iraola’s double pivot, freeing Dominik Szoboszlai and Florian Wirtz to play higher, yet that is a heavy fee for a player only just rebuilding match fitness, with Liverpool fourth and nine points behind Arsenal.

Chelsea’s case is simpler. The division’s biggest summer spenders lost their midfield engine and can justify the price more easily. Arsenal’s patience makes sense, since Rice, Guimaraes and Zubimendi leave no room for a £100m squad player. A Liverpool bid would only inflate the market Chelsea are already shaping. If Iraola wants a January signing, a specialist holding midfielder for far less money does more for the top-four push.

In their previous league outing, Les Olympiens claimed a commendable 2-1 victory over Lens at the Stade Bollaert-Delelis, while Les Manceaux scored late against Monaco on home soil to salvage a point.

Following a dismal start to the current league campaign, losing five of their opening six matches to leave them languishing inside the relegation zone and just one point off the foot of the table at the end of September, Marseille will be delighted with how they have bounced back in recent weeks.

Since their narrow 2-1 loss to back-to-back European champions Paris Saint-Germain on September 20, Les Olympiens have been an unstoppable force, winning each of their previous five domestic matches to rise to fourth in the Ligue 1 table and sit just five points off Les Parisiens at the summit.

The biggest strength of Bruno Genesio’s side has undoubtedly been their free flowing attack, as after 10 league games, Marseille have netted an impressive 22 goals, a tally that cannot be bettered by any other side in the division.

However, Les Olympiens will undoubtedly be disappointed with their performances in the UEFA Europa League, as after four league phase fixtures they have picked up just three points and at the moment reside outside of the tournament’s progression places to the knockout stage.

Having gone unbeaten in each of their previous six encounters with Le Mans, including a 2-1 victory in their most recent meeting at the Stade Velodrome in January 2010, Marseille will be confident that they can continue their fine league form this weekend though and mount a charge towards PSG in top spot.

It has been revealed that after ending their 16-year wait for promotion to France’s top tier at the end of the 2025-26 campaign, beating Bastia 2-0 away from home on the final day to pip St. Etienne to second place, Le Mans will have mixed feelings about their start to life in Ligue 1 this season.

Although they lost just one of their opening five Ligue 1 matches to start the campaign, Patrick Videira’s men have failed to claim a league victory in over two months, leaving them 15th in the table with eight points and only outside of the relegation places on goal difference.

Without a doubt, Les Manceaux’s weakness in the 2026-27 season has been their leaky defence, as Sunday’s visitors have conceded a concerning 19 league goals so far and are one of three sides alongside Lens and Strasbourg that are yet to keep a clean sheet.

Despite previously claiming victory at the Stade Velodrome, posting a famous 3-2 win in September 1994, Le Mans head into Sunday’s match in poor form, facing Marseille as massive underdogs, and knowing they’ll need to pull off another monumental triumph if they want to get their season back on track this weekend.

Le Mans form (all competitions):.

Marseille are still without Italian full-back Emerson Palmieri, who is expected to return before the end of the year from a knee problem, while Canadian midfielder Derek Cornelius continues his struggles with a hip problem.

On a more positive note, Genesio will be glad that a cohort of important first team players including the likes of Pierre-Emile Hojbjerg, Nayef Aguerd and Geoffrey Kondogbia have all returned from the international break unscathed.

Netting an impressive seven Ligue 1 goals so far this season, including one in each of his previous three league outings, Amine Gouiri is undoubtedly Les Olympiens’ dangerman and will be hoping to close the gap to Paris FC’s Lassine Sinayoko at the top of the division’s scoring charts on Sunday evening.

Le Mans are certain to be missing Algerian midfielder Adil Bourabaa and former Everton defender Djibril Sidibe this weekend as the pair are ruled out with ankle and foot injuries respectively.

It remains to be seen whether either Samuel Yohou, who has reportedly sustained a head injury, or young French midfielder Martin Rossignol can fight off issues to feature at the Stade Velodrome too.

After signing from Ligue 2 side Guingamp in the summer, 32-year-old striker Louis Mafouta has been the visitors’ biggest attacking threat this season, scoring a respectable four goals in 10 league matches.

De Lange; Weah, Egan-Riley, Aguerd, Garcia; Hojbjerg, Nnadi; Harit, Abdelli, Paixao; Gouiri.

Le Mans possible starting lineup:.

Kocik; Bamba, Torrente, Voyer; Vercruysse; Buades, Traore, Bretelle, Calodat; Mafouta, Gueye.

Having emphatically bounced back from their early season woes, Marseille will be confident that they can beat any opponent they come up against and continue their impressive rise up the table.

Although Le Mans will be desperate to turn around their poor form, we believe the hosts will be far too strong and are backing them to close the gap on the teams above by posting a convincing victory at the Stade Velodrome on Sunday evening.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • This is a preview of subscription content, access via your institution.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Amazon rainforest is a cornerstone of regional and global carbon cycling1 and is widely regarded and modelled as a perennially evergreen ecosystem2,3. This prevailing view, however, masks substantial fine-scale variation in leaf phenology, limiting our capacity to predict ecosystem responses to climate change. Here by combining 10-m Sentinel-2 observations with machine learning, we uncover pervasive, spatially structured seasonal deciduousness across the basin. In 70.0% of the Amazon, leaf shedding precedes leaf flushing by at least 3 months, creating pronounced asynchrony between deciduousness and greenness seasonality, whereas the remainder reveals near-synchronous phenology. Hydroclimate emerges as the dominant factor associated with this asynchrony across 51.6% of the area, followed by soil properties (33.2%) and light availability (15.2%). Motivated by this widespread decoupling between deciduousness and canopy greenness, we incorporated deciduousness-constrained leaf turnover and the resulting leaf-age demography into ecophysiological models, yielding spatially widespread improvements in the seasonal agreement between simulated gross primary productivity and satellite-derived photosynthetic seasonality across 79.9% of the basin. These findings challenge the conventional view of Amazonian phenology, demonstrating that previously overlooked deciduousness influences Amazonian carbon dynamics. Incorporating these insights into process-based models is essential for refining projections of climate–forest feedbacks in the Amazon and for understanding its ecological functions under accelerating global change.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • The first 11 games of the Serie A season have produced some rather intriguing trends regarding AC Milan’s attacking productivity.
  • MilanNews recall how – after the important win in Genoa before the break – Ruben Amorim emphasised how this Milan team are still far from the final product he envisioned in the summer, especially in the final third.
  • The Rossoneri are improving in possession control and chance creation, but they often remain too far from the opponent’s penalty area for most of the game.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The first 11 games of the Serie A season have produced some rather intriguing trends regarding AC Milan’s attacking productivity.

MilanNews recall how – after the important win in Genoa before the break – Ruben Amorim emphasised how this Milan team are still far from the final product he envisioned in the summer, especially in the final third.

The Rossoneri are improving in possession control and chance creation, but they often remain too far from the opponent’s penalty area for most of the game. This limitation has also affected Gonçalo Ramos, who has been forced to drop deeper, far away from the penalty box.

After 11 league games, Milan are only 17th in Serie A for shots on goal, averaging 11.5 per game. Yet, they lead Serie A in average xG per shot, at 0.145. In other words, the Rossoneri do not shoot much, but when they do it is very dangerous.

It has been revealed that this is also confirmed by the remarkable individual numbers. Adrien Rabiot has scored five goals from 12 shots, with a conversion rate of 41.7%. Diego Moreira is at 40%, Alphadjo Cisse at 38.5%, and Christian Pulisic at 36.4%.

The notable absentee from this ranking is the player expected to score the most: Gonçalo Ramos. The Portuguese has scored just three goals with 33 total shots and 5.35 xG, meaning a conversion rate of 9.1%. These numbers are far from those of his team-mates.

According to recent reports, amorim continues to defend him, emphasising that the problem lies primarily with the team being too deep. Milan must therefore start to generate more territorial dominance, to allow Ramos to operate closer to goal and for him to be on the end of what is clearly quality service being provided.

Chelsea’s £43m Winger Gamble Is Stalling: Should They Accept A Discount?

📅 02 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (415 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Footballtransfertavern

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Chelsea transfer news: Birmingham Live reports that Alejandro Garnacho’s future needs resolving, because the winger has not started a match for Aston Villa and a permanent move depends on certain conditions being met.
  • FotMob lists four Premier League outings, all from the bench, without a goal or assist, while Football365 counts only 95 minutes across seven substitute appearances.
  • It has been revealed that garnacho’s strengths haven’t changed.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Chelsea transfer news: Birmingham Live reports that Alejandro Garnacho’s future needs resolving, because the winger has not started a match for Aston Villa and a permanent move depends on certain conditions being met. Chelsea sent the 22-year-old to Villa Park on a season-long loan in July, with a reported £43m obligation to buy next summer. Neither club has revealed the trigger, and reports link it to appearances.

The numbers explain the concern. FotMob lists four Premier League outings, all from the bench, without a goal or assist, while Football365 counts only 95 minutes across seven substitute appearances. Football Insider claims Villa are prepared to back out of the deal if his form doesn’t improve.

It has been revealed that garnacho’s strengths haven’t changed. His pace, directness and willingness to take on defenders earned a £40m move from Manchester United in 2025. The weakness is end product, and it followed him to London with eight goals in 43 games for Chelsea, only one of them in 24 Premier League appearances. Unai Emery left him out of the squad for the Manchester United game.

Chelsea have no obvious use for him either. Xabi Alonso told him in July that regular football wasn’t guaranteed, and the 3-4-2-1 Alonso favours uses Morgan Rogers and Cole Palmer behind João Pedro, with Pedro Neto and Estêvão competing for the wide roles.

It has been revealed that fotMob values him at about €29m (roughly £25m), far below the €71m peak recorded in August 2024, and Manchester United are reportedly entitled to 10 per cent of any future fee. If the clause isn’t triggered, he returns in July 2027 on a contract running to 2032.

Yes, and soon. Chelsea built the deal to protect £43m, but the clause relies on appearances from a manager who isn’t picking him, so the price drops with every unused substitution. The sporting case for a return is thin. Alonso’s system asks wide players to defend as wing-backs, while Garnacho’s value lies in isolating a full-back, and the £117m Rogers signing already covers the left-sided attacking role.

A mid-£20m sale, even after United’s cut, would still return more than half of the £40m Chelsea paid and clear a contract running to 2032. Chelsea should open talks with Villa in January about a lower fixed fee, or line up other buyers for the summer. A clause that depends on a manager picking a player he has benched was never a safe way to protect £43m.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Cristiano Ronaldo took to social media on Thursday to announce that he had played his last game for Portugal.
  • Industry observers note that "To the Portuguese people, the day has come for me to hand back the No.
  • "I never felt it belonged to me alone, but for 23 years I had the privilege and the responsibility of wearing it, defending it and carrying it with me into stadiums all around the world," Ronaldo said.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Cristiano Ronaldo took to social media on Thursday to announce that he had played his last game for Portugal.

Industry observers note that "To the Portuguese people, the day has come for me to hand back the No. 7 shirt of our national team," the 41-year-old Ronaldo mentioned in a video on his Instagram account.

"I never felt it belonged to me alone, but for 23 years I had the privilege and the responsibility of wearing it, defending it and carrying it with me into stadiums all around the world," Ronaldo said.

The former Manchester United, Real Madrid and Juventus forward represented his country 234 times, scoring 146 goals — making him the men's record-holder for ⁠international ​appearances and for international goals.

He captained Portugal ​to their first major trophy at ​Euro 2016 and led them to the 2019 and 2025 Nations League titles.

In a recent development, "It was not an easy decision, there are decisions that are not ​only with the head. They are also made with the heart," Ronaldo continued in the Instagram post.

"If I ever made you happy, ​if one of my goals ever made you hug someone, forget a worry or feel ⁠proud ​of our country, then it ​was all worth it.".

He also thanked his family, the Portuguese people ​and the teammates, coaches and staff he worked with over his national ​team career.

The Portuguese Football Association (FPF) released a statement expressing its gratitude and respect for the player also known as "CR7.".

"Cristiano Ronaldo has raised Portugal's profile and inspired generations of young people who dream of following in his footsteps; for many of us, he is the greatest player of all time!" it read.

The FPF intends to organize a tribute "in which the fans and the country can one more time applaud and celebrate a player who has given us so much.".

It has been revealed that while his long-rival Lionel Messi ended his Argentina career with a much anticipated farewell match last month, Ronaldo's final appearance may go down as Portugal's 1-0 win over Wales on September 24, depending on the nature of the tribute. Portugal coach Jorge Jesus left him on the bench for the following match and said he wouldn't start the next one.

Ronaldo responded by walking out of the Portugal training camp. He was subsequently suspended and fined by the FPF, but he had been expected to return to Portugal for the November international break.

Like Messi, Ronaldo intends to continue his club career with Al-Nassr in Saudi Arabia.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • The point leaves Fiorentina 15th in the table on 9 points.
  • Industry observers note that the hosts led after four minutes.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Gleison Bremer's equaliser earned Juventus a point at the Stadio Artemio Franchi after they twice fell behind against Fiorentina. Spalletti's side now go into the international break outside the Champions League places, with their next home game brought forward by a day.

The point leaves Fiorentina 15th in the table on 9 points.

Industry observers note that the hosts led after four minutes. Mateo Pellegrino scored, set up by Pedro Goncalves. Nick Woltemade levelled in the 32nd minute from a Randal Kolo Muani assist, and it was 1-1 at half-time.

According to recent reports, fiorentina went ahead again in the 54th minute. Guglielmo Vicario made the first save, but the Juventus defenders were too slow to clear. Alieu Njie forced in the rebound. Bremer then reached a Douglas Luiz corner in the six-yard box before David de Gea could get to it.

Juventus completed 384 accurate passes to Fiorentina’s 273. Fiorentina still attempted 22 shots to Juventus’s 18, and both sides had 6 on target. The expected goals figures, 2.46 for Juventus and 2.14 for Fiorentina, are consistent with a fairly even contest despite the visitors’ control of the ball.

The closing stages could have gone either way. Former Juventus defender Radu Drăgușin headed in from a corner in the 82nd minute. The goal was ruled out because he pushed Bremer with both hands. Near the end, Vicario saved twice in quick succession to protect the point. Juventus also claimed a penalty when the ball struck João Mário’s arm in the Fiorentina area, but none was given.

Referee Andrea Colombo booked three Juventus players. Juan Cabal was cautioned in the 13th minute and Bremer in the 22nd. Kolo Muani was booked for dissent in the 73rd. Christ Inao Oulaï was Fiorentina’s only booking.

Industry observers note that juventus were without the injured Kenan Yildiz, Andrea Cambiaso, Nico González, Manuel Locatelli, Khéphren Thuram and Kamil Grabara. Weston McKennie and Zeki Çelik returned to the squad. Spalletti made three changes in the 57th minute, sending on Zhegrova for Woltemade, Alajbegovic for Boga and Celik for Cabal. Ekhator replaced McKennie in the 78th minute and Gatti came on for Lucumí in the 89th.

Sources indicate that at his press conference at the Franchi, Spalletti said he was not happy because his team does not play at a steady enough level to aim for anything notable. He did praise Kolo Muani, describing him as the player everyone wanted and one he can use as a centre-forward or out wide. Shown a replay of the João Mário incident, he dodged the question and asked, smiling, for a different one.

FT |⌛️| Termina in parità ⚪️⚫️@EASPORTSFC @easportsfcit#FiorentinaJuve pic.twitter.com/Twp629BYvj.

— JuventusFC (@juventusfc) November 8, 2026.

The draw ended a run of two wins, against AZ Alkmaar and Napoli. Woltemade and Pellegrino both received a rating of 8.2 from the data provider.

Recent findings suggest that next up for Juventus is Venezia, who sit 19th on 6 points. When fixture times were first set, that game was pencilled in for Monday 23 November at 20:45 Italian time.

Liverpool Open Talks With Argentine Midfielder: Is He Worth A New Deal?

📅 02 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (388 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Footballtransfertavern

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that liverpool transfer news: Liverpool have opened contract talks with Alexis Mac Allister, according to @tribuna_ftbl, with his current deal running until June 2028.
  • It also reverses the summer, when the club extended Ryan Gravenberch and Dominik Szoboszlai but made no offer to the 27-year-old, something Mac Allister revealed in September while admitting he had stayed despite chances to leave.
  • In a recent development, his form explains the change.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that liverpool transfer news: Liverpool have opened contract talks with Alexis Mac Allister, according to @tribuna_ftbl, with his current deal running until June 2028. The report arrives days after his father, Carlos, told ESPN that no discussions had started, although he hinted at news before the end of the year.

It also reverses the summer, when the club extended Ryan Gravenberch and Dominik Szoboszlai but made no offer to the 27-year-old, something Mac Allister revealed in September while admitting he had stayed despite chances to leave.

In a recent development, his form explains the change. After a poor 2025/26 under Arne Slot, he has become Andoni Iraola’s first-choice midfielder alongside Szoboszlai, pushing Gravenberch to the bench. He has scored once in the Premier League and three times in the Champions League, including the winner against Atlético Madrid, and holds a 7.29 FotMob average rating across 758 league minutes. Liverpool sit fourth.

FotMob places him in the 88th percentile among midfielders for shot attempts, and he has noted the man-to-man system suits him because it demands less communication than Slot’s approach. His weaknesses are just as clear.

His defensive contributions (45th percentile) and aerial duels (46th) sit below the midfield average, and pundit David Lynch has questioned whether his legs have gone in Iraola’s 4-4-2, where two central midfielders cover huge areas. He has also collected four league yellow cards already.

Yes, but not on the terms his summer rebound might demand. Ten league games of good form do not cancel a season in which he looked off the pace, so Liverpool should offer around three years, with wages pitched below the bumper deals Gravenberch and Szoboszlai signed.

The timing still makes sense. With 18 months left, he enters the final year next summer, when Liverpool would face either a discounted sale or a free departure. His FotMob valuation of €66m has almost halved from the €130m peak of September 2025, so selling now would lock in the lowest price.

Iraola also needs a controller to sit beside Szoboszlai’s runs, and no one in the squad does that better. The caveat is that Mac Allister turns 28 next month, so Liverpool must pair him with a quicker partner next summer rather than treat his renewal as the end of the midfield rebuild.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Roberto D'Aversa's Sassuolo tenure begins against Genoa on Sunday, with the Neroverdi in danger of slipping into the relegation zone.
  • The matchday 12 encounter pits two sides separated by four places in the Serie A table, with the higher-ranked Rossoblu chasing a fifth consecutive victory in this fixture.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Seye Omidiora | 20 Nov 2026 21:13.

Roberto D'Aversa's Sassuolo tenure begins against Genoa on Sunday, with the Neroverdi in danger of slipping into the relegation zone.

The matchday 12 encounter pits two sides separated by four places in the Serie A table, with the higher-ranked Rossoblu chasing a fifth consecutive victory in this fixture.

Sassuolo's brief association with Alberto Aquilani lasted just 11 league matches, with the board in Reggio Emilia making another managerial change to arrest the club's poor run of results.

Admittedly, the Black and Greens made a respectable start under the former midfielder, collecting seven points from their opening four games as a three-match unbeaten run followed an opening-day 2-1 defeat at Atalanta BC.

However, mid-September's 2-1 reverse at Monza began a seven-match winless league sequence, and Sassuolo's defensive record under Aquilani made for grim reading.

The Neroverdi conceded a staggering 19 goals across five defeats, losing 4-2 to Frosinone, 2-0 to Como, 6-2 to Lazio, 4-2 to Fiorentina and 3-0 at Roma.

The defeat at the Olimpico proved the final straw for the 17th-placed outfit, who sit just one point clear of the relegation zone and two ahead of 19th-placed Venezia.

That underlines the scale of the task facing D'Aversa, who inherits a side that have conceded 29 Serie A goals, four more than both Monza and bottom-placed Udinese, two of the teams presently occupying the relegation places.

Daniele De Rossi's men will hope that the fresh boss needs time to adapt to his surroundings as they seek to extend the Black and Greens' losing sequence.

The travelling supporters will welcome this weekend's trip, given that the Grifone have claimed four consecutive victories in this fixture, including two at Mapei Stadium.

Beyond those recent successes in Reggio Emilia, the Ligurian outfit enter this weekend as one of the competition's form teams.

Their 2-1 home defeat to AC Milan before the international break ended Genoa's three-match winning streak, during which they stunned Juventus 2-0 in front of their supporters.

Having collected 12 points from their last 18 in Serie A, losing to Roma and Milan during that improved run, De Rossi's men will back themselves to overcome any newly introduced-manager bounce in Emilia-Romagna and claim consecutive away league victories for the first time since November-December 2024, when they beat Parma 1-0 and Udinese 2-0.

D'Aversa has several fitness concerns ahead of his first Sassuolo match: Cristian Volpato, Yeferson Paz, Daniel Boloca, Domenico Berardi and Vasilije Adzic will be assessed before Sunday's clash; however, Fedde Leysen (knee) and Ismael Kone (broken leg) are sidelined.

If three-goal Adzic cannot feature, the new manager will have to rely on Sebastiano Esposito and Armand Lauriente, who have scored twice apiece, to shoulder more of the Black and Greens' attacking burden.

Genoa, meanwhile, will look to Milutin Osmajic and Junior Messias to add to their respective Serie A tallies of four and two goals, while Stephan El Shaarawy has registered two assists in his last three appearances for the Ligurian outfit.

A relatively healthy squad further boosts the visitors' prospects, although Morten Frendrup remains doubtful due to the ankle problem that kept him out of the Rossoblu's defeat to Milan last time out.

Sassuolo possible starting lineup:.

Muric; Walukiewicz, Caleta-Car, Idzes, Doig; Thorstvedt, Matic, Sulemana; Dominguez, Lauriente; Esposito.

Genoa possible starting lineup:.

Bijlow; Marcandalli, Ostigard, Vasquez; Ehizibue, Wiafe, Traore, Ellertsson; Junior Messias, El Shaarawy; Osmajic.

Sassuolo's injury doubts complicate D'Aversa's first assignment, particularly with Berardi and Adzic potentially unavailable to bolster an attack already struggling to compensate for the team's defensive frailties.

Genoa arrive with fewer fitness concerns and a confident Osmajic, suggesting that De Rossi's men can secure a fifth successive victory over the Neroverdi.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Joshua Cole | 20 Nov 2026 21:38, Last updated: 20 Nov 2026 21:43.

Kasimpasa will be looking to extend their unbeaten run when they welcome Alanyaspor to Recep Tayyip Erdogan Stadium on Sunday afternoon.

The hosts occupy fifth place in the Turkish Super Lig standings with 20 points from 11 matches, while the visitors sit 13th with 12 points and will be desperate to end a difficult run of results after losing their last four games.

Emre Belozoglu's sudden departure to Fenerbahce has not affected Kasimpasa, who have continued their encouraging run of form in recent weeks, putting together a five-match unbeaten streak in all competitions to move into contention for a place in the upper half of the Turkish Super Lig table.

The run began with a 4-1 home victory over Samsunspor, before they followed that result with a 1-0 away win against Eyupspor six days later.

They continued their progress with a 3-1 victory over Corluspor 1947 in the Turkish Cup, although their next league assignment proved considerably more challenging as they held Besiktas to a 2-2 draw at home.

Kasimpasa then produced another impressive performance in their most recent league outing, which was Alfred Schreuder's first game in charge, recording a 2-0 away victory over Gaziantep to make it three wins and a draw in their last four league matches.

The Apaches will therefore be confident of continuing their progress against Alanyaspor, particularly as they have yet to lose at home this season, although they have recorded just one victory, with the other four league games ending in draws.

The hosts will also draw encouragement from their recent record in this fixture, having avoided defeat in their last nine meetings with the visitors, winning seven and drawing two, including each of the last five encounters.

Alanyaspor, meanwhile, have endured a difficult period after making a reasonably encouraging start to the campaign, with their recent defeats leaving them in the bottom half of the standings.

Joao Pereira's side began their latest run of league fixtures with a goalless draw against Erzurumspor before suffering a 3-0 defeat away to Fenerbahce seven days later.

They subsequently lost 2-1 at home to Kocaelispor, with their defensive problems becoming more pronounced when they travelled to face Genclerbirligi, where they were beaten 5-0, suffering their heaviest defeat of the campaign.

Their struggles continued in their most recent league fixture, as they lost 2-0 at home to Trabzonspor, leaving them without a league goal in consecutive matches.

Their 4-1 Turkish Cup victory over 12 Bingolspor offered some encouragement between those league defeats, but the visitors have struggled to transfer that attacking performance into their domestic campaign.

Kasimpasa will be without Elson Mendes, who is suspended for Sunday's encounter, while Godfried Frimpong and Kamil Corekci are also expected to miss out through injury.

Kevin Mouanga, Fousseni Diabate and Mortadha Ben Ouanes are among the players carrying fitness concerns, while Andri Fannar Baldursson is also expected to be unavailable after picking up a muscle injury.

Adrian Benedyczak is expected to lead the attack after establishing himself as the club's leading scorer, with Haris Hajradinovic and John-Jules Rak-Sakyi likely to provide support from behind the striker.

Alanyaspor are expected to be without Paolo Fernandes, who is recovering from a muscle injury, while Fatih Aksoy is also a doubt after picking up an injury.

Pereira could therefore retain much of the side that started against Trabzonspor, with Ruan, Hwang Ui-jo and Ogulcan Usluoglu expected to provide the attacking threat for the visitors.

Paulo Victor; Nuno Lima, Aliti, Ozyurt; Hadergjonaj, Gezek, Maestro, Ozdemir; Ruan, Hwang, Usluoglu.

Kasimpasa have shown considerably more consistency than their opponents in recent weeks and have also dominated this fixture in recent seasons, which is why we expect the hosts to secure a comfortable home victory.

At the Stadio Rigamonti-Ceppi, the manner of the defeat was as worrying as the scoreline.

According to recent reports, the opener set the tone. Lecco needed only six minutes to go ahead. Casarotto ran through the middle, got past Corradi and beat goalkeeper Mangiapoco. Lecco held that single-goal lead until half-time.

According to recent reports, next Gen did have one clear opening before the break. In the 40th minute, Grelaud shot from near the penalty spot. Vettorel turned the effort over for a corner.

It has been revealed that massimo Brambilla did not hide from the problems. He told TuttoMercatoWeb that his side struggled against Lecco’s high press. His players found it hard to keep the ball against a team pressing hard and man-to-man.

The coach also admitted that coming back became difficult after the second goal. He stated his players must improve how they read the game and stop giving away goals so easily.

Industry observers note that the table makes the warning sharper. Brambilla’s side sit third from bottom after the defeat, having won just one of their last 12 matches.

The result also matters beyond Serie C. Carnevali has put the youth sector at the centre of the club’s intends.

In a recent development, one player supporters will watch is Destiny Elimoghale, who came off the bench at Lecco. Next Gen had started in a 3-5-2, with Durmisi and Merola in attack. Elimoghale replaced Durmisi in the 40th minute of the second half. The forward was born in 2009. His new contract, announced on 3 November, runs until 30 June 2029.

The next opponents arrive in good spirits. Treviso beat Novara 2-0 in round 13. Romeo scored in the 24th minute, and Paganini added the second in the 59th.

According to recent reports, the next test comes quickly. Next Gen host Treviso in round 14 on Sunday 15 November at 17:30. A trip to Giana Erminio follows on Saturday 21 November, at the same kick-off time.

Russia is back in world sport, but who is drug testing its athletes?

📅 05 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (870 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Fresh questions have emerged over Russia's return to world sport after figures reviewed by DW revealed that only four of the 16 Russian weightlifters competing at this year's world championships underwent out-of-competition testing by the International Testing Agency (ITA).
  • Two-time European champion Anastasiia Romanova, who previously served a two-year doping ban, was among those not tested by the ITA during the first nine months of 2026, according to its quarterly anti-doping reports.
  • Recent findings suggest that by comparison, all 13 members of the North Korean team underwent at least one ITA test during the same period.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Fresh questions have emerged over Russia's return to world sport after figures reviewed by DW revealed that only four of the 16 Russian weightlifters competing at this year's world championships underwent out-of-competition testing by the International Testing Agency (ITA).

Two-time European champion Anastasiia Romanova, who previously served a two-year doping ban, was among those not tested by the ITA during the first nine months of 2026, according to its quarterly anti-doping reports.

Recent findings suggest that by comparison, all 13 members of the North Korean team underwent at least one ITA test during the same period. North Korea, like Russia, has a history of doping violations in weightlifting.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

The ITA, which runs weightlifting's anti-doping program, told DW that it tested all 16 Russian weightlifters "ahead of their participation in the event." DW understands those tests were conducted in Ningbo, China, where the championships are being held.

According to recent reports, in a power sport like weightlifting, performance-enhancing drugs are most beneficial during training, when athletes build strength and muscle mass in the months before competition. Some drugs, such as anabolic steroids, may be harder to detect by the time the competition comes around.

Rob Koehler, head of the athlete-led movement Global Athlete, called the lack of out-of-competition testing "absurd.".

Industry observers note that "Out-of-competition testing is the backbone of anti-doping," Koehler told DW. "Everybody knows there's going to be testing at the event. But not everybody knows when they're going to be tested 365 days a year outside events. It's concerning that the ITA doesn't see this as a red flag.".

Marta Nawrocka, the ITA's spokesperson, said that Russian athletes were among the 10 most-tested nationalities in weightlifting this year. She also defended the fact that only two Russian weightlifters feature in the sport's highest-priority testing pool, saying inclusion is based on performance and risk profiles.

"Russia's history of doping in weightlifting remains an important factor in the ITA's risk assessment and testing priorities," Nawrocka said. "Russian weightlifters remain subject to substantial testing activity.".

Koehler, though, is unconvinced.

"You simply can't treat Russia like any other country," he noted. "It has to have more scrutiny. It has to have more testing. If you don't do that, you're undermining athlete confidence in the system.".

The International Weightlifting Federation did not respond to a request for comment.

Weightlifting was one of the sports most implicated in Russia's state-sponsored doping scandal, which came to light after the 2014 Sochi Winter Olympics. It ranked second only to athletics for the number of positive cases identified by Canadian lawyer Richard McLaren in his 2016 report commissioned by WADA, the global anti-doping watchdog.

Recent findings suggest that the scandal led to dozens of Russian athletes being banned across numerous sports. RUSADA, Russia's anti-doping agency, has remained suspended for most of the past decade.

As a result, its Moscow laboratory cannot analyze urine and blood samples, meaning samples collected by the agency must be sent abroad for analysis under what WADA described as a "strict chain of custody.".

WADA said it continued to monitor RUSADA but had been unable to gain access to the country to review the agency's suspension because of the "ongoing geopolitical situation.".

It added that RUSADA had "collected thousands of samples … including hundreds from weightlifters" so far this year.

"Given the history, WADA remains vigilant when it comes to Russia," James Fitzgerald, WADA's spokesperson, told DW. "We must ensure that no stone is left unturned when it comes to verifying that all the proper testing and other anti-doping activities are taking place.".

Despite being suspended, RUSADA still has the power to investigate and prosecute anti-doping cases involving Russian athletes, which critics find difficult to reconcile.

"It's a compounding problem that WADA is still giving them a free pass when it can't even get into Russia to see what they're doing," said Koehler, WADA's former deputy director general.

"There's simply no oversight and no accountability. And quite frankly, I don't think there ever really has been.".

Critics also argue that ongoing questions over RUSADA's leadership and independence suggest that little has been fixed in the decade since the McLaren report.

Even the International Olympic Committee (IOC), whose president, Kirsty Coventry, supports the full return of Russian athletes, has acknowledged a "lack of confidence" over RUSADA's governance.

Nawrocka said the IOC had "recently entrusted" the ITA with an expanded role within Russia in the run-up to the Los Angeles Olympics in 2028, but did not explain what the role would involve or when it might begin.

In April, investigative outlet The Insider reported that Veronika Loginova, the agency's head, was in a long-term relationship with an alleged FSB officer. The FSB, Russia's domestic security service, played a central role in covering up positive drug tests at the Sochi Games.

Loginova did not respond to questions for this article but dismissed the allegations at the time as "all this nonsense," writing in an email that she believed "sport exists separate from politics.".

WADA confirmed to DW only that its investigations unit was examining the allegations against Loginova and that the inquiry was ongoing.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that manchester United are like John Toshack’s duvet. You fix one problem – being far too vulnerable to conceding goals – only to create another – lacking the threat to score. It is all very Meh United not Man United. The indisputable fact is they are just not very entertaining to watch. They are slow and dull.

Sources indicate that in the end it also points to another thing. The thing highlighted in midweek by Lisandro Martínez after the Champions League defeat at Atlético Madrid: they do not have the strength in depth to compete.

According to recent reports, what they do have appears to not be fit for purpose. Certainly Michael Carrick, the under-pressure manager, is struggling to get the best out of the resources he has.

“It’s like a duvet,” Toshack, the former Real Madrid and Wales manager, famously noted of football. “If you pull it up, your feet get cold. If you pull it down, your shoulders get cold.”.

There will have been times in the last few days, with the intense criticism and scrutiny over his future, when Carrick will have simply felt like dragging that duvet up over his head and keeping it there.

In a recent development, defeat by Leeds United would have been unthinkable. It would have put Carrick under potentially intolerable pressure in what appears to be a pivotal week, with Como away in the Champions League and a home Premier League fixture against Bournemouth in the coming days.

According to recent reports, was this a lifeline or the tightening of the noose for Carrick? Time will soon tell. The relief of avoiding defeat was tempered by the reality of it now being just one win in their opening seven league games – at home to newly promoted Ipswich Town – and they are down in 13th place. It is six games without a win in all competitions.

That is unacceptable and is their fewest number of league victories in a top-flight campaign since 1986-87. Back then they sacked their manager in November and brought in a certain Alex Ferguson.

The hard truth is Carrick needs to start collecting some “Ws” in those results columns. United are already 14 points behind leaders Manchester City and five outside the probable Champions League places. Qualifying again for that tournament must be the minimum expectation.

Ruben Amorim, Carrick’s predecessor, lost his job within 24 hours of the same 1-1 scoreline at Elland Road last season – dismissed after Martínez-like explosive comments again aimed at director of football Jason Wilcox. Carrick will not suffer the same fate after this, but the ice is becoming increasingly thin.

According to recent reports, we have seen this movie before at United. A slow start to the season, a period of drift, falling out of contention, no reaction on the pitch, backing from the hierarchy that becomes increasingly unconvincing. And then a change.

Recent findings suggest that can Carrick, who genuinely does still retain support at the highest level, alter that pattern? Does he have it in him? Is he too passive like his team? Carrick said this draw felt like a “fresh start”, but on this evidence that comment can be classified as wildly optimistic.

It has been revealed that having directed his criticism at the United hierarchy, and specifically Wilcox, the former Leeds winger who was here, over a lack of summer signings, Martínez apologised and was named in the starting XI. But the Argentine only lasted to half-time, withdrawn injured with a tight thigh, and sat watching the second half with his hood up over his head.

What United did sign in the last window was three midfielders – at a cost of £155m – and all three started: Carlos Baleba alongside Andrey Santos with Youri Tielemans in the No 10 role, which meant Bruno Fernandes was pushed out to the left, from where he constantly wanted to come in-field, with Amad Diallo on the right.

Carrick talked of having a “fresh spine” as well as that fresh start. But it did not make for a potent combination even if, further forward, Bryan Mbeumo played through the middle and scored one. He should have scored another.

But beyond that United created little. “It was a dominant performance against Man United,” Daniel Farke, the Leeds manager, claimed. He was right. If one team deserved to win it was his. They had the chances but snatched at them with Anton Stach, in injury time, having a weak shot cleared off the line by Martínez’s replacement Noussair Mazraoui after a mistake by goalkeeper Senne Lammens. Stach had to score.

United were ahead at half-time. Mbeumo had headed wastefully wide when unmarked but did well to force his way past James Justin and meet a low cross from Tielemans to poke the ball home. The way the usually undemonstrative Carrick punched the air in his technical area revealed the pressure he felt. It was something to build on. To gain control.

Recent findings suggest that leeds had started well but did not really pose much of a threat – beyond forcing Lammens to save well from Nico Elvedi’s downward header – and maybe the earlier kick-off subdued the crowd. This was far from a bear pit.

According to recent reports, but after the break, Leeds were comfortably the better side. The nature of their equalising goal, with Dominic Calvert-Lewin too strong and alert for first Baleba and then Mbeumo to fire in from a corner, exposed the enduring softness at the heart of United.

Industry observers note that and that must be addressed by Carrick, especially as he appeared to sacrifice attacking intent by shoring up defensively. But that duvet is looking far too inadequate right now. Or Carrick is making it appear so.

Michael Carrick says he has put on “the headphones” this week in an effort to drown out the noise, but admitted Manchester United have to stop their struggles from snowballing.

United sit just two points above the relegation zone after a 1-1 draw at Leeds left them with just one win from their opening seven Premier League matches.

Carrick claimed the result felt like a “fresh start” after a week in which Lisandro Martínez publicly apologised for criticising Jason Wilcox, the United director of football, and the Old Trafford board.

But the United manager acknowledged their position “doesn’t look too good” and that they must start winning soon to stop the club from entering another doom cycle.

“Listen, we’re not accepting it as everything’s great by any stretch, so I’m realistic with that,” said the United manager, who claimed “the headphones have been on this week”.

It has been revealed that “But sometimes you do struggle, sometimes there’s a bit of it where you have to find a way through it. We haven’t really had to go through that yet [before now] and we have to find a way through it.

It has been revealed that “There has been a cycle at times here over a period of time when it can go in different directions. We’ve got to be stable enough to keep doing the right things for the right reasons as a group, and we’re more than capable of winning football matches.

“I understand the situation doesn’t look too good if you look at it from a certain way, but I’ve no doubts we can go on a good run.”.

United face Como in the Champions League in Italy on Wednesday before Bournemouth visit Old Trafford four days later.

Carrick noted he remains convinced United can still have a strong campaign, despite their worst start to a season for 40 years. I know what we’ve got in the changing room, where we want to get to, how we want to get there,” he said. “We know we can do it.

“We’ve done it for some time, and we feel we’re a better group now, and I do feel that. Sometimes it doesn’t always show, but you get a feeling and I’m encouraged by a lot of things. And if we keep doing the right things, I think we can still have a really good season.”.

Asked if he would be putting the headphones back on this week ahead of two more pivotal games, Carrick added: “Nah, it’s always quiet for me.”.

It has been revealed that martínez was substituted at half-time at Elland Road with a tight thigh just days after his tirade at club executives and Marcus Rashford was left out for “purely tactical” reasons. “Nothing personal, the front players were doing a good job on and off the ball,” Carrick stated. “Everyone is ready for Wednesday.”.

Recent findings suggest that the Leeds boss told Sky Sports: “We are slightly disappointed it is just a point. Overall, I felt it was not necessary to be losing at half time but it is still Manchester United. “We took it as a compliment that we have done many things right over the last month if we were seen as favourites against Manchester Untiedbut we have earned this. We wanted to prove the comments right.

Just 10 months on from Ruben Amorim’s final game in charge of Manchester United, the club return to Elland Road on Sunday afternoon with another manager under pressure and the director of football again in the spotlight.

The difference is Michael Carrick still has a chance to determine the course of his United future whereas Amorim had already sealed his fate after a furious bust-up with Jason Wilcox 48 hours before his last game ended in a 1-1 draw with Leeds and post-match fireworks.

But even for a club never far from a crisis, it seems remarkable to think they are back in a tailspin so soon after Amorim’s sacking in early January.

Good afternoon and welcome to our live coverage of this mouthwatering Premier League fixture between Manchester United and Leeds United at Elland Road.

It has been revealed that quiet week in the world of Man Utd? Don’t be silly. Following a 2-0 defeat in the Champions League against Atlético Madrid in Spain on Wednesday, defender Lisandro Martinez rolled out an extraordinary attack on Man Utd’s director of football Jason Wilcox and the club’s hierarchy because of a dreadful start to the campaign, which has yielded two victories in nine games across all competitions.

The Argentine criticised Man Utd’s recruitment and noted he expected more, but didn’t suggest Carrick was to blame. Martinez has since apologised for his outburst and met with Wilcox, Man Utd chief executive Omar Berrada and Michael Carrick, with Telegraph Sport understanding that he’s free to play today, although his role remains unclear as we all eagerly await the team news.

Carrick is under immense pressure to get a result here in Yorkshire, with last weekend’s 1-1 draw with 10-man Tottenham at Old Trafford condemning Man Utd to their worst league start for 40 years.

Industry observers note that with all eyes on the visitors, Leeds will be licking their lips at the prospect of piling further misery on their beleaguered opponents. Daniel Farke’s side suffered their first Premier League loss last weekend, falling 2-1 to Arsenal at the Emirates after going a goal up, but the mood remains positive after a solid start to the campaign.

Leeds are eighth and the club will be harbouring ambitions of a top-half finish in the Premier League for the first time since the 2019/20 season, with the prospect of qualifying for European football not out of the realm of possibility.

Sources indicate that unlike Man Utd, Leeds have a settled, reliable system that clearly suits their current squad. Elland Road will also be a cauldron of hostility and noise, given the fierce backdrop between these two bitter rivals.

This has all the ingredients to be a thrilling and fascinating watch as we bring you the latest updates, information and drama. Kick-off is at 14:00, with team news coming shortly.

Massimo Oddo has admitted that Francesco Camarda has unquestionable talent, but suggested there has been some impatience regarding his development.

Industry observers note that going into the 2025-26 season, the decision was made to send Camarda out on loan to Lecce, where he had a mixed campaign to say the least. He did score his first ever Serie A goal, but played second fiddle for large spells until a shoulder injury saw him miss an extended period.

Ruben Amorim arrived and decided that he wished to keep the 18-year-old around, believing that he is ready to be the deputy to Goncalo Ramos, the new club-record signing. The Portuguese is struggling for goals, while Camarda is struggling for minutes, leading to suggestions of a new loan in January.

Sources indicate that oddo knows Camarda well having been the head coach of Milan Futuro during their first season in Serie C and then in Serie D following their relegation. Speaking to La Repubblica, he gave his take on the forward’s current situation.

It has been revealed that “The talent hasn’t disappeared, but you have to be patient. I take Camarda as an example, one of the most promising centre-forwards I’ve ever seen,” he remarked (via Calciomercato.com).

“He couldn’t wait and paid the price for his early leap to Serie A. He should have taken a more gradual path, like Pio Esposito. In general, I’m concerned about the excessive power of agents.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Joshua Cole | 20 Nov 2026 21:40, Last updated: 20 Nov 2026 21:42.

Konyaspor will be looking to halt their recent slide down the Turkish Super Lig standings when they welcome Besiktas to Medas Konya Buyuksehir Stadyumu on Sunday afternoon.

The hosts sit 15th in the table with eight points from 11 matches, only outside the bottom three on goal difference, while the Black Eagles occupy fifth place with 19 points from 10 games and will be hoping to maintain their push towards the top of the standings.

Konyaspor have endured a difficult run of results in recent weeks, winning just once in their last six league matches and struggling to find consistency in the final third.

Ilhan Palut's side began that sequence with consecutive goalless draws against Kasimpasa and Istanbul Basaksehir before suffering a 1-0 defeat away to Amed SK.

They then recorded a 2-0 home victory over Genclerbirligi, but that proved to be their only success during the period as they suffered consecutive defeats against Galatasaray (4-0) and Samsunspor (1-0).

Konyaspor were particularly disappointing in their defeat away to Samsunspor just before the break, failing to take anything from a match against a side sitting second-bottom and enduring a losing run.

The result further highlighted their struggles in front of goal, with the hosts having scored just six times in their opening 11 league matches, an average of fewer than one per game, while they have failed to find the net in seven of those fixtures.

Konyaspor have scored four of their six goals and collected seven of their eight points on home soil, although they were thrashed by Galatasaray in their last home game and now face a Besiktas side that have beaten them in their last two league meetings.

The hosts did manage to defeat the Black Eagles 1-0 in their most recent encounter, although that victory came in the Turkish Cup.

Besiktas, meanwhile, have enjoyed a more productive campaign, collecting seven wins, one draw and three defeats from their opening 11 league matches to remain within reach of the leading teams, sitting six points behind league leaders Galatasaray.

Vincenzo Italiano's side are also unbeaten in their last three league games, a sequence that began with a 2-0 home victory over Istanbul Basaksehir before they were held to a 2-2 draw by Kasimpasa.

Their subsequent European fixture saw them suffer a 3-2 defeat against Celtic, but they responded positively three days later by recording a convincing 3-0 home win over Genclerbirligi.

Dusan Vlahovic was particularly influential in that victory, scoring twice as the Black Eagles returned to winning ways in the Super Lig and demonstrated the attacking quality that has made them one of the more productive sides in the division, with only four teams scoring more than their 23 goals.

However, the visitors have struggled on the road, winning just one of their five away league matches and failing to win any of their last three, during which they have recorded one draw and two defeats.

Besiktas Turkish Super Lig form:.

Konyaspor will be without Adil Demirbag, who is recovering from a cruciate ligament injury and is expected to remain sidelined for the rest of the season.

Chidozie Awaziem is also unlikely to feature after sustaining a muscle injury, while Marko Jevtovic is working towards regaining full fitness and faces a late assessment.

Ugurcan Yazgili is another concern after picking up a hamstring problem, leaving Palut with defensive and midfield decisions to make.

Mostafa Mohamed, Diogo Goncalves and Ebrima Colley are among the attacking options available to the Konyaspor manager, although Enis Bardhi is expected to miss out through suspension.

Besiktas will be without Umit Akdag, who is recovering from a broken wrist, while Fabio Miretti is also expected to miss the match with a shoulder injury.

Emmanuel Agbadou is not expected to return until later in December as he continues his recovery from a knee problem, while Orkun Kokcu is also sidelined with a foot injury.

Konyaspor possible starting lineup:.

Gungordu; Andzouana, Baniya, Bosluk, Masuaku; Toth, Ibrahimoglu; Colley, Goncalves, Dompe; Mohamed.

Besiktas possible starting lineup:.

Nubel; Murillo, Taylan Bulut, Topcu, R Yilmaz; Ndidi; Trossard, S Ozcan, Olaitan, Fakili; Vlahovic.

Konyaspor have struggled to produce consistent attacking performances this season, and although Besiktas have been inconsistent on the road, their attacking quality should be enough to overcome the hosts' defensive resistance, with Italiano's side expected to secure a comfortable victory in Konya.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Serie A's sporting judge fined Juventus for holding up the start of the game at Fiorentina, and handed the hosts the same penalty. No Juventus player is banned, so Spalletti has a full squad for Venezia, though Bremer and Kolo Muani now have a sanction against their names.

Sources indicate that juventus came out of their trip to Florence with a bill rather than a ban. Serie A sporting judge Gerardo Mastrandrea punished the club for an unjustified delay to the start of the first half at Fiorentina. The hosts were handed an identical penalty for the same hold-up.

The rulings came in Official Communiqué No. 60, published in Milan on 10 November 2026. Mastrandrea reached them at a meeting that day with Stefania Ginesio and AIA referees’ representative Carlo Moretti. The communiqué states that the fines, including those given to individual club members, will be charged to each club’s LCA league account.

Only one club paid more than Juventus. Como received the heaviest club fine of the round, €10,000, for delaying the start of the second half by about two minutes. The judge treated that as a repeated offence. Genoa were fined €4,000 and Lazio €3,000.

It has been revealed that more important for Spalletti is what the ruling did not contain. No Juventus player was suspended. Only two players across the league were banned after round 11, according to Corriere dello Sport. They were Parma’s Ndiaye and Frosinone’s Bracaglia, each for one match.

Industry observers note that that leaves Spalletti with a full squad for the first game after the international break. He will want every option. The match in Florence, scheduled for Sunday 8 November at 20:45, was assigned to referee Colombo, with Maresca as fourth official and Di Paolo on VAR.

Industry observers note that it ended in a draw that left Juventus seventh on 18 points, Eurosport reported. Fiorentina stayed two points clear of the relegation zone. Spalletti said afterwards that his side “are not consistent” and sometimes lose their way over very little.

Industry observers note that the ruling did leave a mark on four first-team figures. Randal Kolo Muani, Gleison Bremer and Juan Cabal each picked up their first sanction of the season. Spalletti’s assistant Marco Domenichini did too.

Bremer and Kolo Muani are key players for the coach.

In a recent development, the count has only started, but it will matter as the season goes on. The fine itself is small, and the sporting picture is unchanged.

No other side has conceded more goals than Eyupspor this season, with their tally standing at 30, while they have also scored just three times, the fewest in the league.

Mustafa Dalci noted after the defeat to Kocaelispor that his side are entering a period in which they must start collecting points, but their prospects look bleak ahead of another difficult away fixture, particularly as they have conceded a league-high 19 goals on their travels.

Their head-to-head record against Trabzonspor offers little encouragement either, with Eyupspor yet to win any of their four previous meetings, drawing one and losing three, while they have failed to score in all four encounters.

European shares fell sharply in early trading on Friday as a global sell-off fueled by concerns over artificial intelligence stocks spread from Wall Street to Asia and Europe.

Fears of curbs on AI data-center spending have added to investors' concerns after Democrats won control of both chambers of the US Congress.

It has been revealed that the pan-European STOXX 600 index dropped 1.6% in early trading, wiping out its gains for the week. Most major European markets fell more than 1%, with media, healthcare and retail stocks leading the declines.

European markets had previously weathered the week's turbulence better than their Asian and US counterparts because of their more limited exposure to AI stocks.

Earlier, Japanese and South Korean shares tumbled after a massive selloff in tech stocks on Wall Street the previous day.

It has been revealed that tokyo's benchmark Nikkei 225 index fell 5.5% in early trade, while Seoul's tech-heavy Kospi index slid as much as 8.8%, triggering a circuit breaker which suspended trading for 20 minutes. Taiwan's benchmark TAIEX index was also down more than 8%.

Asian tech giants including Samsung Electronics, SK Hynix and Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Firm (TSMC) have borne the brunt of the artificial intelligence-related selloff.

Samsung plunged nearly 10% while SK Hynix slid over 11%.

Chip-related shares in Japan also took a beating, with Tokyo Electron stock trading down around 9% and Kioxia shedding 13%.

US markets were hammered on Thursday by a sharp retreat in tech stocks, particularly those involved in the buildout of artificial intelligence infrastructure like data centers.

The tech-heavy Nasdaq fell 5.52% and shed as much as $2.5 trillion (roughly €2.23 trillion) in market value, while the broader S&P 500 index plunged 4.4%.

The rout occurred as investors grow increasingly anxious about the colossal AI spending aims and whether they will eventually produce commensurate profits.

The results of the US midterm elections, which saw Democrats seize control of both houses of US Congress, added to the concerns.

A number of Democratic governors-elect campaigned on slowing artificial intelligence development and promised to stop or pause the construction of data centers amid growing public opposition to such projects.

"It's pretty clear there's been a real shift ​in sentiment," Michael McCarthy, chief executive for Australia and Upcoming Zealand at online brokerage Moomoo, told the Reuters news agency.

According to recent reports, "Market turning points are often accompanied by strong disagreement, and that indicates up in the market ​by huge swings in either direction," he remarked. "That's what we appear to have had — and last night's emphatic sell-down suggests that is the direction that we're now headed in.".

Erzurumspor took the lead against Rizespor through Ibrahim Diabate, but they were unable to hold on to their advantage as the hosts turned the contest around, leaving Serkan Ozbalta's side with consecutive defeats after they had collected 10 points from their preceding four matches.

Despite those setbacks, the hosts will be encouraged by their home performances this season, having beaten Konyaspor, Eyupspor and Samsunspor while suffering defeats against Galatasaray and Corum, the latter being their most recent appearance in front of their supporters.

They will be keen to rediscover the defensive organisation that helped them secure those three victories without conceding, particularly against a Goztepe side that has demonstrated considerable attacking quality in recent weeks.

This will be the fifth Super Lig meeting between the sides, with Erzurumspor picking up two wins, drawing one and losing one of the previous four, although they have lost their last two encounters against the visitors, one in the Turkish Cup and the other in the second division.

Goztepe, meanwhile, had been enjoying an impressive run of results before their latest setback, winning four consecutive league matches as part of a six-game unbeaten streak to establish themselves in the top half of the table.

Stanimir Stoilov's side began that sequence with a 4-0 away victory over Eyupspor before recording a 2-1 win against Kocaelispor and a 2-0 home triumph over Corum.

The visitors then produced one of their most impressive performances of the campaign by defeating Fenerbahce 2-1 away from home.

However, their winning streak came to an end just before the break when they suffered a 2-1 home defeat against Istanbul Basaksehir, with Juan finding the net but the hosts ultimately unable to prevent their opponents from taking all three points.

Goztepe nevertheless have an away unbeaten run to protect, with Goz Goz having gone four games without defeat on the road, winning their last three and drawing the other.
